Your money does not rely on large quantities but on a good reputation. Income is stable and secure, but the overall scale is not very high; it rises slowly, and after middle age, when your reputation has accumulated, it will step up noticeably. Your most natural way of earning is turning the learning in your head into money, for example as a consultant, in training, in professional services such as law or medicine, or by writing books. You do not spend ostentatiously and can hold on to money. Money leaks away in two places: you value loyalty to others so much that money and effort keep going out the door, and you hold so firmly to your own ways that you miss opportunities you could have earned from.

Your money mainly follows position. Income from salary, rank and title is stable and not small; getting rich fast through speculation or gambling is not your road. You are not exactly short of cash, but your spending is also large and savings build rather slowly, because you value appearances, like to buy things that are good and expensive, and keeping up your image all year round costs quite a lot. Another place where money drains away is that you trust your own judgment too much, and when a whimsical decision turns out wrong, the loss is often not small. Your wealth fortune comes rather late; after middle age, as your position rises, money is noticeably more generous, and it grows steadier the further on you go.

Your money mainly follows position. Income from salary and a stable rank; getting rich fast through speculation or gambling is not your road. You are not exactly short of cash, but savings build slowly, because you are particular about how you spend: brands, taste, and being well turned out when you go out; handbags, jewellery and looking after your image are expenses that are not cheap all year round. In your household you are rarely content to be a passive record-keeper; most of the time you yourself manage the money, and you have a habit of keeping a portion apart from the joint account that no one can touch. Your wealth fortune comes rather late; only after middle age, as your position rises, is money noticeably more generous.

Your money is rarely the kind that arrives evenly month by month. Your salary rises and falls with your career; your truly large sums are mostly unplanned money, arriving one lump at a time through connections, opportunities and investments. If the chart also meets the Fire Star or Bell Star, this kind of incoming money comes even more easily, but what comes fast also goes fast. For those who meet the Fire Star, ups and downs before thirty are normal, and money is truly accumulated mostly after thirty. You earn money easily but keep it with difficulty; food and fun, clothes and travel - any one of them is enough to drain your funds dry.

Your money is saved up bit by bit. Your family gives you little capital, and results become clear only after middle age; hoping for a windfall to change your life is unrealistic. In daily life you are actually very good at calculating - prices, discounts and membership cards are all at your fingertips - yet the money still does not stay: the leaks are concentrated in four items, eating out, taking care of yourself, taking the children out and buying things for the family, all of which make you and your family comfortable and which you spend on without regret. You mostly do not fight to manage the household money: you look after the daily life and the atmosphere at home, and hand large investments to your partner.

Your money comes in waves. It is not a small even stream: when it is good it comes in very fast, and when it is slack it can stay slack for a very long time. Money mostly comes from busy, crowded places, where your talent and reputation can be turned into money - performing, design, consulting and opening your own shop all count. Your ability to manage money is rather weak, and when you see something beautiful or enjoyable you easily let go; the real big leaks are spending for the sake of feelings, impulse shopping, and the costs of lawsuits and settling troubles.

Your money comes in waves. When it is good it comes in fast, and when it is slack you have to endure for a while. Money mostly comes from your talent and charm, and design, performing, consulting and your own brand are all paths for you. You manage money rather weakly and let go most easily over beautiful things; clothes, art objects and home decorations are often large expenses. What you most need to watch is spending for the sake of feelings: once you have committed seriously, you easily spend large sums for the other person.

Your money rises and falls erratically. When it is good it comes in strongly, and when it is slack it is truly slack; do not use a passing spell of plenty or shortage to guess your whole life. Fixed income follows the swings of your career, and windfalls often appear in times of change, so catching the right moment helps more than head-down toil. Your skill at earning is finding business opportunities in change: foreign trade, pioneering sales, new technology, and professional services built on one craft are all your roads. Your ability to hold money is rather weak; when your mood is good you spend freely, and when you hit a low your purse is suddenly tight.

Your money rises and falls erratically. It follows the ups and downs of your career: when it is good it comes in strongly, and when it is slack it is truly slack. Your skill at earning lies in three words, going out: cross-border e-commerce, translation, international trade, overseas consulting and developing in several cities are all your natural roads to wealth, and what you fear most is staying in one place doing a job that never changes. In spending, you are more impulsive than most people, ordering as soon as you like something and regretting it afterwards. You value the sense of security of your own account very much and are not very willing to be merely the bookkeeper for the family.

Your money is accumulated slowly. It comes from professional services, a fixed salary or work related to aesthetics, steady like a small stream flowing evenly. Houses and real estate are your real purse; speculation of the kind that comes fast and goes fast is not your road. You value quality of life and are willing to spend on housing, food and travel, and your ability to keep money is average. There are two leaks: one is large spending on family and partner, the other is investment decisions made when emotions are running high. When your feelings are harmonious and your family is peaceful, your wealth fortune runs smoothly too.

Your money is accumulated slowly. Your family gives you little capital, in the early years it is hard to see large sums, and only after middle age does it gradually take shape; hoping for a windfall to change your life is unrealistic. Your main income comes from work and salary, stable but not fast. Your real way of earning is reputation: do a certain thing so well that people trust you, and customers bring in customers. The leaks are very fixed - things that make you comfortable such as food, travel and relaxation; money usually slips away bit by bit like that.

Your money comes from saving up, not from fighting for it. Your income mainly comes from steady work and savings accumulated day by day; because you spend with moderation, your assets thicken on their own over time - a small but even stream - and after middle age you will have a fairly full hand. Your ability to keep money is strong and you do not spend rashly on impulse, but sometimes you save too much, begrudging even what should be spent on health and living. There are two real places where money drains away: one is being too conservative, so that you do not dare to jump in even when a good opportunity is laid right in front of you; the other is big spending on feelings and family.

Your money comes from saving up, not from fighting for it. Your income mainly comes from steady work and savings accumulated day by day; you spend with moderation, so your assets thicken on their own over time, and after middle age you will have a fairly full hand. You are very good at managing a family's accounts, and your husband and children both benefit from your planning. What you value is real security - a home, deposits, insurance - and not outward show; you also keep a reserve of your own. There are two places where money drains away: being too conservative and missing good opportunities, and big household expenses that were not planned in advance.

Your money comes in very steadily. You do not worry about food and clothing, relying mainly on income from your main job and accumulating bit by bit. You rarely have money falling from the sky or a big sum arriving at once; money mostly follows your rise in rank and is brought by benefactors. You spend with moderation and do not lose big sums on impulse, but sometimes you are so conservative that you miss good opportunities. There are two places where money leaks: spending too much on social relationships, and not being able to refuse others, so that time and resources are lost for nothing. Your assets rise steadily, and after middle age you are clearly better off.

Your money comes in very steadily. You do not worry about food and clothing, relying mainly on your main job, following your rise in rank and brought by benefactors, and you rarely have money falling from the sky or a big sum arriving at once. You spend with moderation and do not lose big sums on impulse, but sometimes you are so conservative that you miss good opportunities. The biggest blind spot is in the family: you spend on family members without hesitation, but weigh and reweigh spending on yourself; you also think a married couple's money should naturally be shared, so you hold almost no portion of your own. After middle age your finances will become clearly more generous.

Your money comes fast and goes fast. When it is good a large sum comes in, when it is bad there is a large shortfall, and the ups and downs are very clear. You are someone who shoulders everything alone and charges forward, and the money you earn is hard to hold on to; earning it but being unable to keep it is your biggest hurdle. Fixed income relies on your ability and solid work; the part earned through opportunities is greater than other people's because you dare to take risks, but you can also easily lose a large sum on investments made too aggressively. Your biggest drains are impulsive bets, spending money out of pique, and acting too fast with contracts that are not written clearly.

Your money comes fast and goes fast. When it is good a large sum comes in, when it is bad there is a large shortfall, and the ups and downs are clear. Your money is made by running out and charging ahead; finance, sales, starting a business and foreign trade - fast-paced roads like these suit you best - and earning it but being unable to keep it is the most typical hurdle. There is a blind spot worth mentioning: you are especially harsh on yourself, and in the busiest years of your career you get by with what you wear and use; besides, the more you earn, the firmer your voice at home, and your husband easily feels pushed aside.

Your money comes with ups and downs. It is not the kind where you save a sum and then lie back to enjoy it, but depends on whether your mind keeps up. Working steadily for others, receiving a salary or taking jobs for a fee is your foundation; money earned through luck cannot be kept. Turning your mind into money is your most natural road - teaching, consulting, drawing up plans and writing all count. Your ability to earn is stronger than your ability to keep money; with many ideas, you split your money in many directions, and in the end none of them grows. In the early years your income swings widely, and only after forty, when you have accumulated enough experience, does it gradually stabilise.

Your money comes with ups and downs. It depends on whether your mind keeps up, not on saving a sum and then lying back to enjoy it. Working steadily for others, receiving a salary or taking jobs for a fee is your foundation; money earned through luck cannot be kept. Turning your mind into money is the most natural - teaching, consulting, drawing up plans and writing all count. Your ability to earn is stronger than your ability to keep money: you are an expert at researching goods and comparing prices, but the more you look the more you buy, and subscriptions, skincare and small items adding up one by one are invisible leaks; when you are unhappy inside, you are all the more likely to use shopping to redirect your attention.

Your money comes from many mixed sources. Your salary rises and falls with your career, and money arrives unevenly. Earning money is not hard for you; the hard part is keeping it. Clothes, handbags, beauty, travel, restaurants a notch better - you spend on every one of them willingly, and money comes from lively places and goes out through lively places. What is most worrying is that at your peak you are busy making things dazzling, leaving no capital in the books, and by middle age your life is beautiful but your deposits are very thin.

Your money is tied directly to your gift of speech and your professional skill. You do not rely on your family to give you anything, you have to build a career with your own hands, and the money has to be earned in busy, crowded places. Stable income comes from professional services and selling knowledge, and as your skill grows your income grows; side opportunities come through connections and information, and you move faster than others. When your ambitions are too high and your words too big, you can instead lose all that you have saved in one go.

Your money is tied directly to your gift of speech and your professional skill. You do not rely on your family to give you anything, you have to build a career with your own hands, and you earn in busy, crowded places. You manage money by researching: before buying a financial product or evaluating a project you compare again and again, and fine words cannot lead you by the nose. The places where money is most easily lost are, first, fees for settling disputes and lawyers, and second, researching for too long, so that when you have thought a good opportunity through it has already passed.

Your money is earned through reputation, steady and secure. The upper limit is higher than you think, so do not rush to put a ceiling on yourself. What is most special about you is that you have a purse of your own: you earn on your own, spend on your own and plan your own old age, and whether you marry has little effect on your sense of security. Money is lost in two places: you value loyalty to others so much that money and effort keep going out the door, and you are shy about speaking up over money, so in the long run you set your prices too low.

Your money is earned through ability, with a full foundation. Money earned from work and your specialty is the main source, and as long as you are willing to put in the effort you see the return. Your road to wealth is to exchange your ability for income, and the more specialised and the harder to replace you are, the better the money comes in. Windfalls need an exceptional opportunity and cannot be counted on. You do not spend recklessly for the sake of appearances and you keep your money, it is only that sometimes you save too much and live more tightly than your income requires. Money is added steadily, not doubled overnight, and by middle age your foundation will be very thick.

Your money is earned through ability, with a full foundation. Money earned from work and your specialty is the main source, and as long as you are willing to put in the effort you see the return. You spend practically, your interest in jewellery and brand names is far less than other people's, and you like to turn money into things you can touch: a house, gold and fixed-term deposits. You have a very strong urge to control the household money, and only when it is in your own hands do you feel at ease; the responsibility you carry for your mother's family is also heavier than other people's. Money is added steadily, not doubled overnight, and after middle age your foundation is fairly thick.

What you lack is not the ability to think but the ability to stop. A suggestion is to set deadlines for decisions: decide small matters on the spot, think about big matters for three days at most, choose one when the time is up, and fix it if you chose wrong. Practise telling yourself one sentence: other people's discomfort is their own business; you may feel for them, but you do not need to carry it for them. When you are with others, ask whether they need your help before deciding whether to step in. At work, choose one or two things to do for the long term and persist for three to five years, which is more realistic than spreading yourself across five shallow things at once.

Your ability to gather wealth lies in steadiness. Money comes from professional services, a fixed salary or work related to aesthetics, saved bit by bit, and you do keep what you save. Houses and real estate are your real purse; speculation of the kind that comes fast and goes fast is not your road. You know how to manage a life, calculating closely while still keeping your quality of life. Money flows out mainly toward family and children - when spending on them, the part you most easily forget is your own.

You are quick-witted, and your heart is delicate too. Behind what someone says, you hear the meaning at once. Your greatest strength is standing at the side devising plans and arranging everything so it runs smoothly, the kind of strategist who keeps the whole operation moving. Your road to a living leans toward the secure: positions with a fixed salary and brain work, such as civil service, internal affairs, schools, consulting, education and technical research, suit you best. The difficulty lies in feelings - you are too sensitive, and a tone of voice or an unanswered message can play out as several scenes in your heart, small matters growing bigger the more you think, and you tire yourself out first. What you need is not someone who creates surprises every day, but someone who puts you at ease so that you do not have to guess.

Your mind turns fast, and you see through people and things very clearly. You often come up with angles that others have not thought of. Your greatest strength is flexibility: the moment the environment changes, you find a new direction faster than anyone. The position that suits you best is devising schemes, making plans and serving as a staff adviser; brain-work jobs such as public service and internal affairs are the most natural, and money follows this road too - working for others and drawing a stable salary is the steadiest, while money earned through luck cannot be kept. Your weak point is thinking a lot and doing little: you turn one matter over and over, and by the time you have thought it through the moment has passed; you change your mind quickly, so others easily find you not steady enough. You have a hot temper but a soft heart, you get along with everyone in conversation, yet others often cannot guess what you are thinking.

You are gentle by nature and do not like to compete with people. Wherever you go, you quickly find a rhythm that makes you comfortable. Your greatest capital is popularity: anyone beside you feels at ease, so for things that take many people joining forces to achieve, you are often the most crucial glue, and working with others succeeds more easily than shouldering it alone. Inside, you actually have opinions and ambition, you are just too lazy to bring them out in front of people to fight for. Your weak point is being too easily satisfied: when it is worth fighting, you are used to giving way a step, and over time you are seen as having no views of your own; your decisions are also slow to warm up, and being pressed to settle on the spot is when you are most likely to spoil things.

You are gentle and quick to smile. Wherever you stand, the atmosphere lightens, and people beside you do not need to be on guard. You are clever, learn fast and do not like to compete with others, and in your family and circle of friends you are often the peacemaker. In love, this gentleness is your greatest capital: the other person is mostly drawn in by your amiability, and your romantic path is smoother than most. Your weak point is being too easily satisfied: once life is passable you do not want to move, and in your career you often need someone to give you a push before you advance. One more thing to be careful about - you care so much about harmony that in relationships you easily give up your own thoughts bit by bit until none are left.

What you need to learn is to soften in the places where you should. At work it is fine to keep pushing forward, but do not carry everything alone; whether someone beside you is willing to help decides how far you go more than how capable you are. In love, try changing “I say it and that is that” into “let us discuss it”, and leave the other person an area where you do not interfere. Also, allow yourself to show weakness in front of those close to you; this will not reduce your ability by half, and instead makes your strength more approachable.

What you need to practise is not modesty in words. What you need to do is admit two things: your judgment is sometimes wrong too, and your self-respect does not need to be propped up by making others be quiet. When someone contradicts you to your face, do not rush to argue back; hear them out, then ask one question: “Which matter are you pointing to?” Each week choose one small thing and deliberately do it someone else's way once. When your heart feels choked, do not push on; saying it out loud saves strength and is not a loss of face.

You know many people of many kinds, with a pile of close friends of uneven quality. This is your most valuable ability: the people you know can be turned into opportunities and resources. The trouble is also here: many people stroll the streets and drink with you, but few can step up when the moment is truly critical; the more impressive and capable someone looks, the more clearly you need to see them before you entrust anything. Among men, an especially large number have feelings for you; when you get along, they become benefactors and business partners, and when you do not, they become entanglements that will not let go.

You speak in an orderly way and think deeply. Whether eloquence or gossip weighs more depends on whether Great Gate is Temple, Prosperous or Fallen; yours lies between those two ends, so no clear conclusion can yet be drawn. But this mouth is also a burden: one wrong sentence can be turned over in your mind for three days, and a small misunderstanding can torment you for half a year. Your suspicion is not groundless; you simply look too closely, reading ten layers of meaning from a single expression, so you are not easy to cheat, and also hard to be truly at ease. The pit you fall into most easily is walking into a dead end: when you cannot make sense of one matter, you stop there and speculate over and over, and in the end do nothing.

Your words have an edge. This is not necessarily ill will; you simply have a natural ability to strike straight at the key point, which makes it a little hard for the other person to parry. This eloquence is an advantage at work, but at home it often turns into destructive force: you rarely lose an argument with your partner, but after you win, neither of you is happy. Your mind is deep, you like to investigate, you have a stubbornness about secrets and truth, and you can trace three layers into something others see as nothing, so you are not easily deceived and also easily sink into doubt you cannot escape. Crowded, talkative places are actually your home ground; the edge just has to be drawn into your area of expertise.

You take the road of living off position. Sitting in a position with a title and the deciding voice, you achieve more than doing the execution below. State agencies, the judiciary, the management tier of large companies and the senior ranks of financial institutions are the places that suit you best. You are good at setting direction, and do not like and are not good at petty details, so you need capable people to carry things out for you. Compared with starting out on your own, you suit borrowing momentum on a large platform, rising steadily on rank and a fixed salary. Your income is tied to position: the higher the position, the thicker the money, and promotion improves your income more than changing jobs does.

You get along well with your siblings. Everyone has a temperament that does not quarrel often, the atmosphere at holiday gatherings is harmonious, and when you actually work on something together, your side is a plus. The trouble lies in boundaries: siblings are all easygoing with each other, and things such as borrowing money, helping out and standing as guarantor are often agreed to on impulse, only to be regretted later.

You get along well with your siblings. Everyone has a temperament that does not quarrel often, the atmosphere at holiday gatherings is harmonious, and when you actually work on something together, your side is a plus. The trouble lies in boundaries: siblings are all easygoing with each other, and things such as borrowing money, helping out and standing as guarantor are often agreed to on impulse, only to be regretted later. When transformed to Taboo (obstruction), the bond easily cools, and entanglements over money are the most hurtful.

You live in harmony with your siblings. Everyone has a temperament that does not quarrel often, and when something comes up you lend each other a hand. But whenever there is a difficulty in the family, the first person thought of is often you - borrowing money, asking you to mind the children for a while, asking you to introduce a job, and you almost never refuse. After you marry, it is the same with your sisters-in-law: your gentleness is liked in the family, but the ones who know best how to cry and make a scene are the ones who most easily get something out of you.

You have a very deep bond with daughters. Mother and daughter are as close as sisters, a rare kind of mother-child bond, and it is also common to have a daughter or to have a daughter first. Your greatest strength as a mother is understanding the small thoughts in your child's heart, especially the hard-to-voice feelings of a daughter in adolescence. Your childbirth is usually fairly smooth, and during the postpartum month there is mostly family to care for you.

The bond between you and your sisters is especially heavy. Older and younger sisters are often your deepest female allies for life, and the sincere words you say to them are the most thorough. After you marry, in getting along with your sisters-in-law, your gentleness is very well liked and you easily become the place where everyone pours out their feelings, but you are also easily worn down.

The bond between you and your mother is especially deep. She is your greatest emotional anchor; the way you are with your mother will also unconsciously carry over into the way you are with your wife and your daughter. Your father influences you comparatively less, but is always a steady support. At work, you often get along especially smoothly with female bosses.

You are so close to your mother that you are almost inseparable. She is your greatest emotional anchor, and also the template for how you will later be a mother. If mother and child are in harmony, you have someone holding you up behind you all your life; if they are tense, you may spend many years reconciling with her shadow. After you marry, living with your in-laws, you easily compare your mother-in-law with your own mother, and the comparison brings disappointment.

The relationship between you and your parents is one in which you must argue things out with each other all your life. Anything can be discussed, and any small matter can also make you fall out. Your bond may be rather thin, with an early departure from home or living far away for a long time, rarely close to your parents. Your way of speaking carries something of your family, worn in by living together day after day, and is not fixed by fate.

The relationship between you and your parents is rather cool. This is not a lack of love, but that you are naturally not good at putting feelings into words. Leaving home early and seeing little of each other is normal for you. The usual background tone of your childhood is your father's strictness and your mother's silence, and you learned early to say nothing and carry things yourself. After you marry, living with your in-laws, you also cannot fake an obedient look, and forcing it only makes you suffocate.

The relationship between you and your parents is rather cool. This is not a lack of love, but that you are naturally not good at putting feelings into words: you miss them in your heart, say nothing with your mouth, and do not take the initiative in action either. Leaving home early and seeing little of each other is normal for you. The impression your father left on you is mostly just two words, strict and orderly, and much of the pressure in your growing up came from him. There is also another situation: your parents say little to you, but at critical moments they steadily support you, giving capital and connections.

The relationship between you and your parents is, all your life, snagged on words. A single sentence from an elder can be your greatest support and can also be your deepest wound. Your bond may be rather thin, with an early departure from home or living far away for a long time, rarely close to your parents.

The bond between you and your elders is rather faint. It is not that the feeling is poor; mostly you see little of each other and each lives in a different place. Your parents are often people with stories of their own: a special occupation or an unusual life experience; the atmosphere at home is also more complicated than in an ordinary home, and there may be old debts that are hard to explain, old romantic matters among the elders, or growing up with your grandparents when small.

Your bond with your elders is rather faint, mostly seeing little of each other and living far apart, each with their own life. Your parents are often people with life stories, and the atmosphere at home is more complicated than in an ordinary home. What deserves the most mention is the relationship between you and your mother: the entanglement between the two of you is especially deep, and she may be both the person closest to you and the wound that hurts you most.

You have a decisiveness and a willingness to take on tasks. While others are still hesitating, you have already acted. This makes you thrive at work, but measured against the previous generation's expectations of women, you are often called too brash and not soft enough. You do not know how to act coy, and it is hard for you to yield the limelight to others and quietly be the good wife behind the scenes - not that you do not want to, but you cannot do it, and forcing it feels awkward. So in marriage you often unintentionally end up in the leading position; it is not that you want to seize it, it is simply your nature. Your popularity is very good, and in your heart you actually want to be taken care of too, but you have never asked.

You have a charm that makes people look twice. This is not necessarily a matter of how beautiful you are, but of a lively, agile air and a wide road, and you are never short of people around you. This charm is both a gift and a test: you attract others easily, but only Greedy Wolf in the Pig and Rat palaces counts as true peach blossom, so in matters of love you cannot guess at entanglements just because you see Greedy Wolf. It is not that you are unfaithful, only that you are naturally sensitive to what is new, and walking the old road for a long time will feel stifling. Also do not let your gentle appearance fool you: inside you have a very hard ruler, and once you have decided on someone, no one's advice does any good.

You have an air that makes people want to look again. It is not the sweet kind, but the kind that is measured and not easy to see through. You have your own standards and do not follow along with others. You are emotional and sensitive, with a special ability to judge beauty, but this emotional nature is also a burden: your feelings swing widely, and today you may cry over a song and tomorrow turn cold over a single remark. When you love, you hold nothing back, but once the feeling is cut off, that pain takes a very long time to digest. Quite a few people take notice of you, and your relationships therefore often become complicated.

There is a stream of fire in you, and your emotions swing widely. As soon as the fire flares up, your body reacts with it: you easily feel internal heat and cannot sleep well. To know which part of the body deserves more attention, look at which palace in the whole chart gathers the most malefic stars, then match that palace's earthly branch to an organ (Rat gallbladder, Ox liver, Tiger lungs, Rabbit large intestine, Dragon stomach, Snake spleen, Horse heart, Goat small intestine, Monkey bladder, Rooster kidneys, Dog pericardium, Pig triple burner), rather than matching by the element of the Integrity star in the Health palace. Your health and your mood are basically one matter: when you are angry, stifled or have failed in love, you decline very quickly. Alcohol and strongly flavoured food will make this fire stronger.

The magnetism about you is very strong. You have your own allure and skill, and easily leave an impression on others. In love you are the one who takes the initiative, with enthusiasm, and you like thrills and novelty, but once a relationship has stabilised your enthusiasm easily fades, and you must deliberately nurture it to go far. Good popularity does not mean choosing the right person, and keeping your judgment amid the bustle is what matters most. This is the foundation brought by your birth year; which decade and which year get activated needs a further look at your periods of fortune.

Beside you there are always a few people with stories of their own. People with talent and skill, and people with complicated romantic histories, all like to gather around you. On this road of yours, whether you have many or few friends does not matter; whether your circle is clean does. The brightness of Integrity in this palace decides whether those willing to put in effort for you come early or late. Whenever friends have romantic troubles they come to you to judge, and in the end you get pulled in yourself.

Beside you there are always a few people with stories of their own. People with complicated romantic histories, people in the arts, and people with unusual trades all like to lean toward you. Friends with something on their mind come to you for advice, and over time you become other people's romance adviser, and as a result get drawn into their feuds and wear yourself down greatly. The brightness of Integrity in this palace decides whether those willing to put in effort for you come early or late. Whether your circle is clean matters more than whether you have many people.

Around you there are many people of stature. Among your friends and subordinates there are quite a few with status, position and rather dignified connections. The old books say that Emperor in this palace means “forming a capable rank, and when prosperous it governs the making of wealth”: under your hand you can gather a group of people who can be used, and who even earn money for you. The same book also places the Friends palace as a Fallen position for Emperor, saying “even if helped, it is not a blessing”; both views exist side by side, so when employing people do not bet everything on others. These people carry great stature, and keeping up airs may instead cost you people's goodwill.

You are someone who acts with moderation and has your own standards. Your air is clear and bright, you are not easy to get close to, and others mostly treat you with respect rather than familiarity. You have good skills and a wide road, and the paths of the arts, law and finance can all be walked. In love you are serious and not easily stirred, and once you have decided, you are very steadfast; your charm is that others are drawn to you, not that you go out to tease anyone.

Your temperament leans toward the firm. You act decisively and are not used to depending on anyone to live; with Martial in the Spouse palace you start a family a little later, and when you meet someone you are sure of, you give yourself more time. This is not a bad destiny of any kind, but that you ask a lot and refuse to settle for a stopgap. The other person must truly win your admiration in some respect before you are willing to show your soft side. The person who suits you best is calmer than you and better at managing money than you, so the two of you can advance together, rather than one depending on the other.

You are someone who cannot sit still. You always carry a streak of impatience; if your home is noisy, messy and busy with people coming and going, your temper grows the longer you stay. To you, home is a charging station, not a place for socialising: lots of guests, a lively living room and people moving about the house all the time will exhaust your body and mind. As for the family property, with Seven Killings meeting Punishment and Imprisonment it is hard to keep.

This firmness of yours is capital. Put to use in your career it is very beneficial, and you do not need to wear it down to please anyone. You only need to patch one gap: in front of your family, allow yourself to say, “I'm a little tired.” Showing softness does not mean losing; it is only the door through which the other person can step in. When you are with others, listen to the end before you judge, and do not rush to a conclusion. After twenty or thirty years of being tough, still letting a gentle person come close to you without being scared away is harder than winning, and also worth more.

The thing you are most likely to lose out on in life is not daring to speak up for yourself. You fight for your family's interests without a moment's hesitation, but when it comes to yourself you always step back. Practise starting with small things: when dividing things at home, say which share you want; when the pay you deserve at work is at stake, bring it up directly; for a place you do not want to go, say you are not going, without making up a reason. The moments when you say no for your own sake are the starting point from which the people around you begin to truly respect you.

You suit places with fierce competition and heavy pressure. The tougher the battle, the more spirit you have. Taking charge, making decisions and leading people are your natural strengths, and only in such positions is your energy put to full use. Purely clerical or purely administrative positions will blunt you; the path that suits you has real authority and calls for drive to break through, for example the military, the police or law enforcement. You push forward fast and do not fear difficulty, but your management style is somewhat rigid and can easily put pressure on your subordinates.

You suit a position that carries a title, where your word is enough. State agencies, the judiciary, the management boards of large companies and senior leadership of financial institutions all suit you; you are good at setting direction, impatient with trivial details, and need capable people to help you carry things out. Your career path is usually smoother than your romantic path, and you would find it hard to be content with only a role at home. The difficulty is particular to women: the years of having children often coincide with the years when your career is breaking through, and there is an invisible ceiling on the way up. Your presence at work is both an advantage and a hidden danger: subordinates respect you but dare not truly follow you, and male peers either avoid you or quietly compete with you.

You meet events calmly and know how to reason. You have a maturity beyond your years, and the more chaotic things get, the steadier you stay; you are the kind of person others want to find for advice at a critical moment. Your heart is clean and you hide nothing, you look gentle, but on matters of principle you give no ground at all; however hard the situation, you find a way through. The price is that you weigh right and wrong too heavily and easily measure others by your own standards, which puts some pressure on those around you. Friends come to you mostly for opinions rather than for fun; your circle is not wide, but they are all people who can truly help. You feel you should help people and pass on experience, and as a result you take every task onto yourself.

You build your reputation on professional ability and on helping people solve problems. You do not rely on grabbing the spotlight; the more you do that is useful to others, the more you rise. Law, healthcare, education, religion, consulting, public welfare, and government posts such as the judiciary, diplomacy and supervision all suit your path very well. In a group you are the one who devises plans and holds the line, the most clear-headed when things are chaotic; the weakness is a somewhat cold manner, so people dare not come close. The benefactors who help you are mostly older and knowledgeable, and a single introduction can change your direction.

Integrity in the Life or Career palace belongs to the martial-official line. So you suit assisting, enforcement and disciplinary work in settings with a set system. The “Complete Book” also says that when Minister or Integrity meets Ram Blade, it is easy to get entangled in lawsuits and penalties; when disputes arise, step back first.

Emperor is of the “official seal, official sash” type, meaning you are born carrying office and authority; whether as a military or a civil official, it is the path with status and rank. Emperor, together with Sun and Martial, is also counted as a benefactor star, so over a lifetime you easily meet benefactors and have help when trouble comes. Earning through proper income, that is, working for others and receiving a fixed salary, raising your income through rank and position, is smoothest; a sudden urge to speculate or take risks is not your strong suit. The saying that circulates outside, “noble but not rich; it needs Prosperity to be complete,” is not in the ancient books; the original text of the “Complete Book” is “If Treasury, Minister, Left Assistant, Right Assistant, Literary Talent and Literary Arts, the benefic stars, gather, there is no one who is not noble. Otherwise, it governs great wealth,” which in plain words is: when Treasury, Minister, Left Assistant, Right Assistant, Literary Talent and Literary Arts, all the benefic stars, are present, no one fails to become eminent and noble, and even if not reaching eminence and nobility, they are mostly very rich. So whether Emperor has both status and money depends on whether there is enough help, not on being born with status but no money.

This combination is called Emperor and Treasury Seated in Their Proper Place, meaning the emperor star and the wealth vault sit in their own correct position: your status can rank among the foremost and you have the bearing of a high official. Someone with this pattern later reaches a status on a par with the Three Terraces, a person at the monarch's side; throughout life, rank and emolument flourish, where rank refers to social standing and emolument to wealth. But even this good pattern can run into trouble if the Decade is not good, so the Decade must be checked as well. People with this life pattern have a square, full face, composed manners and words that carry weight, and they spend generously yet with moderation. At work they are naturally pushed into management, but they are not as aloof and proud as Emperor alone in the Life palace; with Treasury present they understand better how to cooperate.

Strategist follows proper income, that is, working for others and receiving a fixed salary; that is the steadiest road to wealth for Strategist. Income coming from knowledge, skills or planning suits best, while constantly changing investment directions loses money. Focusing on one or two channels for earning is much better than casting a net everywhere.

When the Life palace holds Minister, it is the type with high rank but no real authority. When a Decade reaches Minister, that ten years is the same: for example, being deputy HR director but unable to rise to director, or when others become department heads you become deputy head, always the deputy; a Yearly meeting it is read the same way. This reading method does not apply to the Career palace; Minister falling in the Career palace cannot be read as a lifetime as a deputy. Being reliably dependable is your greatest career strength, trusted by superiors and often supported by benefactors; when it meets Literary Talent, Literary Arts, Left Assistant and Right Assistant, you have both power and reputation, and a full life; the ancient books say you can “rise to the rank of duke or minister”, meaning holding very high office.

Treasury is a civil-official star and also the star of teaching; very many people with Treasury in the Life palace become civil servants or teachers, or even both. State agencies, banks, insurance, administration in large enterprises and the education sector all go smoothly. Your style is conservative and steady, standing firm on system and seniority, and the older you get the more you are valued.

One reading holds that Greedy Wolf in the Children palace means only one child; the “Complete Book” gives a different number, and the two views stand side by side. The ancient books say “Temple or Prosperous: two children, early punishment and clash”, meaning that when Greedy Wolf enters the Temple (a star in this position has great strength) there are about two children, and punishment and clash show early. Children may be showy and fond of enjoyment when young, and the later the years, the better the achievements; “first indulgent, then steady” is the usual way, meaning first letting go, then settling down.

Martial and Greedy Wolf are both martial-official stars and both wealth stars; sharing a palace, they are a martial-official star and a great wealth star in one. For a woman: once the pattern is formed, she is a heroine among women, fierce in action and bold enough to gamble. This life pattern has both the hard, decisive nature of Martial and the many talents and skilful touch of Greedy Wolf.

Martial and Greedy Wolf are both martial-official stars and both wealth stars; sharing a palace, they are a martial-official star and a great wealth star in one. For a man: being born in the daytime suits this pattern best, taking the military or police path with real authority, and travelling and working away from home is even more beneficial. This life pattern has both the hard, decisive nature of Martial and the many talents and skilful touch of Greedy Wolf.

Greedy Wolf governs peach blossom; all pleasures and indulgences such as drink, lust, money, competing to win and gambling are attributed to Greedy Wolf. People with Greedy Wolf in the Life palace easily act on feeling, regardless of everything, that is, once the urge strikes they do not care. Paired with the power of the emperor star, what they want is not only rank and authority but also satisfaction both material and spiritual.

Although this pattern carries an ill reputation, such as dying by the roadside (the “Tai Wei Rhapsody” writes “Seven Killings and Integrity in the same position: a corpse buried in the middle of the road”), when the stars are strong it can make you the head of a region, holding military power like a general, and it cannot be lumped together with the sudden-accident type of Integrity with Army Breaker. Seven Killings also appears with Army Breaker and Greedy Wolf in the palace's trine and opposite palaces (the palaces shining in from other palaces), meaning great change, a love of pioneering, and an unwillingness to live an ordinary life; life will have many ups and downs, and high-pressure fields such as the military, the police, competitive sport and starting a business suit you. However, the “Complete Book” also says that when Seven Killings sits with Integrity in the Life or Body palace (another key position in the chart), you must watch out for injuries to the hands and feet, so do not be too harsh, and do not risk your life by going into dangerous places.
Treasury has no ability to resolve misfortune, and its good fortune hides ill luck; when you meet Treasury, do not feel reassured because of it.

Moon carries proper income, suited to a fixed salary in a state agency or a stable organisation, taking the civil-official path rather than a martial post. If the palace's trine and opposite palaces (the palaces of the chart read together with the palace itself) also show Strategist, Harmony and Heavenly Beam, forming the Strategist, Moon, Harmony, Heavenly Beam pattern, then you are even more the type to do administrative work, with a gentle temperament; only if Fame, Power and Prosperity gather will business come into play.

Martial is the number one wealth star and Treasury is the star that guards wealth; they are very good at managing money. The ancient books say of Martial: “firm in nature, decisive, upright of heart and not venomous,” meaning a hard temperament, quick to settle on a decision, and harbouring no ill intent. Note that someone with Treasury in the Life palace is gentle and decent but calculates a good deal, and is not necessarily a good person.

Emperor with Seven Killings in the Life palace is mostly an only child or the eldest, with no one above them, meaning no one above to shelter them and no one to press down on them, so they must be their own master. This person is hot-tempered, big-eyed, suspicious, headstrong, unwilling to lose and unwilling to settle, with both nerve and strategy, daring to take risks without being reckless; suited to starting a business, the military, the police, finance, surgery, and work that calls for decisive judgement.
Put simply, the Body palace is the acquired side of life, showing who has the greatest influence on them in later life.

This kind of person is decent, humble and gentle; the books record an honest and steady appearance, no worry about food and clothing, plain speech, work without deceit, a soft heart on seeing someone in trouble, and stepping in to defend them on seeing someone do wrong. They treat people properly, distinguish right from wrong clearly, and find it very hard to endure injustice.

Moon carries proper income, suited to a fixed salary, taking the civil-office path rather than a martial post. People with Moon in the Life palace have refined sensibilities and a strong sense of beauty, demand a lot of their living environment, and have an affinity with houses and real estate.

You work with relationships as your foundation; you are the lubricant of the team, standing firm through coordination and a good name, suited to services, education, healthcare, the arts, fields related to children, and every field that needs patience. If the Life palace and the three other related palaces gather Strategist, Moon, Harmony and Heavenly Beam, forming the Strategist, Moon, Harmony, Heavenly Beam pattern, that is a very good pattern, suited to working in a state agency or school with a fixed salary; only if Fame, Power and Prosperity gather will business come into play.

You work with spirit, your emotions are clear, and you easily act on impulse when deciding; in love you invest very deeply, so you are also easily hurt or caught up in disputes, and you need reason to balance your passion. Integrity and Greedy Wolf sitting together in the Life palace, both stars Fallen, is a combination called the self-destruction pattern; falling in the Life palace it means you are born carrying a tendency to destroy yourself, although this temperament is also formed gradually in later life and is not something you are born with. The suffocating feeling of the “Prisoner” in Integrity needs to be released in a positive direction, meaning poured into artistic creation, legal work, political ambition, things that call for both passion and respect for principle.

You work with spirit, your emotions are clear, and you easily act on impulse when deciding; in love you invest very deeply, so you are also easily hurt or caught up in disputes, and you need reason to balance your passion. Integrity and Greedy Wolf sitting together in the Life palace, both stars Fallen, is a combination called the self-destruction pattern; falling in the Life palace it means you are born carrying a tendency to destroy yourself, although this temperament is also formed gradually in later life and is not something you are born with. The suffocating feeling of the “Prisoner” in Integrity needs to be released in a positive direction, meaning poured into artistic creation, legal work, political ambition, things that call for both passion and respect for principle. For a woman: Integrity and Army Breaker sitting together in the Life palace, this kind of martial-official star in a woman's chart means a very tough character and very strong independence and self-reliance.
Your older siblings are mature, like half a teacher.
Your siblings are not many but are talented; affection and interests should be separated clearly from early on.

Your siblings play a very heavy role for you. They are mostly outgoing and decent, working in positions that involve meeting people, such as state agencies, schools or the media. With Sun Prosperous or in the Temple position (great strength), your siblings can be a pillar for you. When things go smoothly for them you benefit too; when they meet setbacks you are easily dragged along by the effects.
You have two or three siblings, loyal and trustworthy but without opinions of their own.
You have few siblings, mostly not getting along, and dealing with each other in a practical way.
You may have five siblings, but this palace is not especially helpful.
Your siblings do not get along; if you go into business together, it is best to spell things out clearly first.

Your siblings are many-talented, lively, strong in peach blossom, with many friends, the type who are “the joy of the whole family.” But the ancient books are very cautious about the number of people and the bonds in this palace: “Greedy Wolf Temple or Prosperous: two people; in the Fallen position, half-siblings by different mothers,” meaning that with Greedy Wolf in the Temple (a star in this position has great strength) there are about two siblings, and falling Fallen (weak strength) they should be siblings by different mothers (the original text says “different wombs”). Adding Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void or Earth Robbery, the ancient books also judge “lonely.” The number of siblings is generally not large.
Your siblings are easy to live with, and business partnerships with them are effective.

Your siblings are loyal and honest. The ancient books say Minister in the Siblings palace is “peaceful, with two or three people,” meaning the number is not large, about two or three, with little major conflict among them, the type of support where “at a critical moment they can lend you money”; as partners they are also reliable, administrative-style collaborators and fairly good assistants, but they lack the ability to lead, so the direction has to be set by you. When Left Assistant and Right Assistant are both in the Siblings palace, the siblings are more numerous and more helpful; the ancient books say that Right Assistant “sharing a palace with Treasury, Minister, Emperor, Literary Talent or Literary Arts gives four or five people,” meaning that Right Assistant sharing the palace with Treasury, Minister, Emperor, Literary Talent or Literary Arts can mean four or five people. On meeting Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void or Earth Robbery, the ancient books say “meeting malefic stars, there are none at all,” and also say “lonely”: no siblings, or lonely. On meeting Earth Void or Earth Robbery, the “seal” of the Siblings palace is damaged, so be especially careful with partnership papers and with signing as a guarantor.

Your siblings are gentle in temperament and live together smoothly, with little major conflict. The books write that Harmony in the Siblings palace entering the Temple (great strength) gives about four or five people. Adding Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void or Earth Robbery, the ancient books say “few people, should live apart, not in harmony”: few people, not in harmony, and living apart suits them. When Harmony transforms to Taboo (obstruction), the ancient books also judge “few people, should live apart, not in harmony.” With Harmony in the Siblings palace, partners are easy to talk to and willing to cooperate, but both sides are easygoing and the drive to charge ahead often lacks a breath, that is, the motivation is insufficient, so it is best to divide the work clearly from the start. With Taboo, the bond between siblings grows thin and the cooperation exists only on the surface; change the phrase “anything is fine” into “let's set one goal together.”

Your siblings are gentle in temperament and live together smoothly, with little major conflict. The books write that Harmony in the Siblings palace entering the Temple (great strength) gives about four or five people. Adding Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void or Earth Robbery, the ancient books say “few people, should live apart, not in harmony”: few people, not in harmony, and living apart suits them. With Harmony in the Siblings palace, partners are easy to talk to and willing to cooperate, but both sides are easygoing and the drive to charge ahead often lacks a breath, that is, the motivation is insufficient, so it is best to divide the work clearly from the start.

Your siblings have strong, independent characters, each minding their own business, with little warmth between them and a rather thin relationship; “meeting only at the New Year” is common. The books put it very bluntly, saying Seven Killings in the Siblings palace “governs loneliness and clash,” meaning the sibling path leans toward solitude and mutual help is hard; only when it falls in the four palaces of Rat, Horse, Tiger and Monkey can there be three siblings, and even then they are “not in harmony and should each live apart,” meaning it is hard for them to get along, and if each lives their own life there is less trouble. If it meets Literary Talent, Literary Arts, Left Assistant and Right Assistant, the affection and help between siblings improve noticeably. In partnerships, the other party is mostly also domineering, and when two strong people come together they must settle who is higher, so I advise signing a contract first and drawing clear boundaries, changing the thought “brothers and sisters don't keep accounts” into “brothers and sisters especially must settle accounts clearly,” otherwise a later falling-out will look very ugly.
Your siblings have many talents and skills.

Your siblings are gentle and refined, rich in feeling, and rarely quarrel roughly. Moon is a yin star representing women, and among your siblings you are usually closer to your sisters, and there is often a female member who carries more weight in feeling or in money. The books write that Moon entering the Temple (entering the Temple = a star in this position has great strength) gives five siblings. When the Siblings palace shows Fame or Power, the ancient books say “Fame and Power together, four or five people”: there are four or five siblings. On meeting Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void or Earth Robbery, the number is halved, and the ancient books say “also clash, should live apart, back to back”: there is clash, and living apart suits them. Partners are refined and sensitive, good at handling complicated relationships, and very good collaborators in terms of “soft power,” meaning they do not rely on hard confrontation but on communication and human feeling to get things done.

The bond with your siblings is somewhat thin; volume one says of Army Breaker, “in the Siblings palace, flesh and blood like Orion and Antares,” meaning siblings are like the two constellations Orion and Antares, where one rises as the other sets, each in a different place, seldom meeting. However, the books say that Army Breaker entering the Temple (entering the Temple = great strength) can give three people, so do not flatly judge that there is no bond. Adding Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void or Earth Robbery, the books judge “lonely.” Partnerships also change often; the people you work with have strong pioneering power but do not hold steady, and easily split and rejoin again and again.
You rarely see your siblings, and partnerships with them change often.
Your siblings are all strong, each living their own life; in a partnership, state the rules first.
Among your siblings, you are closer to your sisters.
Among your siblings there is an older one who is dependable.
Among your siblings there is one who is respectable in the outside world, with a bright, outgoing temperament.

Among your siblings there is one with a bright, outgoing temperament and a fairly high social standing; you deal with each other openly and transparently, with little private calculation, and mostly meet in public settings. The ancient books say Sun entering the Temple (entering the Temple = a star with great strength) in the Siblings palace is usually three people, and the siblings can help get things done. Adding Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void or Earth Robbery, the original text of the ancient books is “clashes more, reduced by half”: the clash is heavier and the number of people is halved.

Among your siblings there is one who is mature and steady; an older sibling has the bearing of an elder and gives you a hand at critical moments. The verse in the “Complete Book” says of Heavenly Beam, “in the Property or Siblings palace, if you obtain it, blessings arise of themselves,” meaning that when Heavenly Beam falls in the Property or Siblings palace, blessings come on their own, which is exactly this kind of protection. Partners are mostly seasoned and steady too, companions who share the load. But the books speak more realistically: entering the Temple (great strength) gives two siblings in harmony, and there may also be many people who do not share the same mother and do not get along. Meeting Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void or Earth Robbery as well, the ancient books give a single word, “few”: even fewer siblings.

Among your siblings there is one who is mature and steady; an older sibling has the bearing of an elder and can give you a hand at critical moments. The verse in the “Complete Book” says of Heavenly Beam, “in the Property or Siblings palace, if you obtain it, blessings arise of themselves,” meaning that when Heavenly Beam falls in the Property or Siblings palace, good fortune comes on its own, which is exactly this protection. Business partners are mostly seasoned and steady too, companions who share the load. But the books speak more realistically: entering the Temple (strong) gives two siblings in harmony, and there may also be many people who do not share the same mother and do not get along with each other. Meeting Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void or Earth Robbery as well, the ancient books give a single word, “few”: even fewer siblings. With Fame (reputation), your siblings use their learning and reputation to support your good name.

With Treasury in the Siblings palace, the “Complete Book” says directly “Treasury: five people,” meaning about five siblings. Master Xi Yi also says Treasury “takes siblings as ordinary,” meaning that for Treasury this palace shows at an ordinary level: the siblings are stable and steady, with few big ups and downs, but they do not especially give you a hand either. As for partnership, such a partner is good at keeping a business going, managing the books, controlling risk and administration, which suits long-term stable cooperation best; guard against being too conservative and missing an opportunity, and also against murky accounts.

With Emperor in the Siblings palace, the ancient books' verdict is “has an older brother to rely on,” meaning that among your siblings there is usually one with a higher standing who backs you, and in real difficulty you will mostly turn to that person. The number of siblings is counted by the ancient books according to the star sharing the palace, and they may not share one mother (the original text is “or born of different wombs”). Adding Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void or Earth Robbery, the original text of the ancient books is “clash and harm; if there, there is little harmony”: among siblings there is clash and harm, and even if they exist they are not in harmony. If you cooperate in work, your partner has a strong presence and everyone has their own opinions, so it is best to state clearly the division of work and who makes the decisions, lest both want to be in charge and neither yields.

First, set boundaries for your emotions. You can help with other people's difficulties, but their feelings are not your responsibility. Take stability as the main thing for income, and only when you have energy to spare put it into solid things such as property; before a large investment, find a calm person to go over the accounts for you, and do not decide on feeling alone. When pressure rises, do not force yourself on; give yourself a day or two of quiet to recover. As for matters between your mother and your wife, speak plainly and directly early on.
Bitter first and sweet after, thinking a great deal all your life, with an affinity for religion and fate studies; what you need to practise is learning to settle down.

In the Temple, your partner is bright and open, and romance goes smoothly; Fallen (weak strength), your partner is hot-tempered, or romance is drawn into matters of honour; volume one says “in the Fallen position meeting malefic stars, harm to the wife is not good,” meaning that Sun Fallen and meeting malefic stars is unfavourable for the spouse.

In the Temple, your partner is bright and open, and romance goes smoothly; Fallen (weak strength), your partner is hot-tempered, or romance is entangled in matters of honour; volume one says “in the Fallen position meeting malefic stars, harm to the wife is not good,” meaning that Sun Fallen and meeting malefic stars is unfavourable for the spouse. For a woman with Sun Fallen in the Spouse palace, you need to tell whether it means a couple who rarely meet and are often apart (the husband is frequently away) or a parting by death; this must be judged from your own face reading, and the chart alone cannot tell them apart. For a woman: Sun represents the husband, and shows his career and public image; the husband is mostly of extraordinary bearing, but busy with his career, and his time with you is limited.
In the Temple, you are content and happy; Fallen and meeting malefic stars, body and mind are both weary.

The malefic stars are relatively most concentrated across the whole chart in the **Tiger palace** (Harmony transformed to Taboo, Earth Void) → corresponding to the organ **lungs**
