With Martial in the Career palace, the Complete Book says “Martial in a Temple position, sharing the palace with Literary Talent, Literary Arts, Left Assistant and Right Assistant, a military post stands out and ordinary people receive blessings; meeting Fame, Power and Prosperity, an official of wealth; with Greedy Wolf, an official of corruption”. One view holds that Greedy Wolf and Martial, besides being military officer stars, can also govern the wealth stars. Executive ability and willpower are your greatest strengths, and the harder it gets the more you open up a road.
With Martial in the Career palace, Martial governs both the military officer and the wealth star.

With Army Breaker in the Career palace, the book says “Army Breaker in a Temple or Prosperous position, a military post excels”, meaning that in a Temple position (this star at full strength in this position) you stand out most on a military-post path. One view holds that Army Breaker in the Rat or Horse palace forms “the hero star in a Temple position” and can bring a military officer career, referring to occupations such as soldier, police, judge and diplomat. Meeting Literary Talent and Literary Arts means “prominent and distinguished”, meaning both reputation and standing rise; adding Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star and Bell Star means “ordinary”, with unremarkable achievements; sharing the palace with Emperor means “a name shaking the world”, a far-reaching reputation; sharing it with Integrity means “a scholar does not last long, clerical work is the finest”, meaning purely civil posts do not last long, and practical affairs in fact suit you best.

With Emperor in the Career palace, one view ranks Emperor among the “official seal, official sash” stars, meaning it is born carrying official rank and authority, and whether as military officer or civil official it counts as this star. This person suits government bodies, the judicial system and the leadership tier of large companies, suits sitting in command rather than charging to the front line oneself, and is good at setting the big direction. The most suitable positions are the kind that “need the backing of authority”, meaning positions where a title and standing must support you; the more official the title and the larger the foundation, the more it can bring out your strengths.

With Greedy Wolf in the Career palace, one view ranks Seven Killings, Army Breaker and Greedy Wolf all as military officer stars, and also holds that Greedy Wolf in the Horse palace is not a peach blossom star but a military officer star. The old books say “Greedy Wolf in a Temple position meeting Fire Star and Bell Star, a military post holding great power”, meaning that when Greedy Wolf is in a Temple position (this star at full strength in this position) and meets Fire Star and Bell Star, a military path can hold great power. The old books also say “in a Fallen palace, an official of corruption”, meaning that when Fallen (weak force), holding power makes it easy to be led by the nose by gain, and you must always keep this limit.

Arrange regular health check-ups for your mother, and do not wait until she says she is unwell before acting. In some matters you should be a bridge, not a messenger. When your mother and your wife each tell you things that are not about the other, take them in from each side and do not pass the words along as they are. Note one more thing: do not carry your dependence on your mother over unchanged onto your wife. She is your partner, not a second mother. When your mother is older, spending more time with her and chatting is more useful than buying things.
The type of person who works for real, speaks little, decides quickly, and does more than he says.
The family fortune is prosperous, and most prosperous in the part you build up yourself.

Home weighs more on your heart than you think. From how the living room is arranged to how the dining table is set, you need a presentable look, and only when the house pleases the eye can your whole being relax. As for family property, with Minister in a Temple or Prosperous position there is a share. In decoration you like a classic style that lasts to the eye, with wood, warm colors and orderly tidying; fashionable styles from the internet do not stay new to you for more than a few days.

The home is arranged to be cozy and comfortable, family life values quality, and you do not chase luxury but must live comfortably. With Taboo, quarrels easily arise at home and the joy of living drops; take the initiative to keep the family in harmony, and turn “it will probably get better” into “I will improve it right now”, meaning do not wait, start right away.
The atmosphere at home is tense, and there is a lot of moving house and changing homes.

The house and the family estate are mostly something you must earn yourself. You are meticulous about where you live, and your home often has taste and a story; the ornaments, colors and furniture all carry a flavor that does not follow the crowd.

The house and the family estate mostly depend on what you earn yourself. You have your own meticulousness about where you live, and your home often has taste and a story; the ornaments, colors and furniture all carry a flavor that does not follow the crowd.

The old house and old capital in your family mostly cannot be kept. You do not need to worry either. The estate that belongs to you is earned back and bought back by yourself. A house to you is more like an asset that can be swapped at any time, and you do not have to put down roots for life in one place.
Old family capital cannot be counted on, and money must be earned again from scratch by yourself.

The houses and capital left by the elders of the family are mostly something you cannot keep. You do not need to worry either; the part of the estate that belongs to you is bought by yourself. Your feeling about home leans towards a temporary place to stay, not somewhere to root for life: today this place seems perfect, and a few years later you find it unsuitable.
Great Gate + Right Assistant means subordinates support the career of your gift of speech; a team can expand your influence.
Great Gate + Earth Robbery means the gift of speech is robbed; what you say gets lifted by others and turned into their idea.
Great Gate + Earth Void means the gift of speech turns to nothing; however well you speak, no one listens, and you need to change your way of communicating or change your platform.
Great Gate + Heavenly Leader means a male noble helper who “turns gossip into eloquence”; at a key moment in life an elder awakens you to the wisdom of speech.
Great Gate + Left Assistant turns the speaking energy of Great Gate into the influence of a team; it suits being a speaker, coach or public figure.

Great Gate + Literary Talent means you can both speak and write; journalist, writer, teacher and lawyer are best. “Great Gate meeting Literary Talent and Literary Arts” is the classic noble pattern leaning towards speech and opinion.
Great Gate + Literary Arts is the strongest combination of “Great Gate entering language-leaning professions”; host, debater and negotiator are best.
Great Gate + Fire Star means heavy fiery quarrels; speaking bluntly offends people, and you need to cultivate the habit of “pausing for three seconds first”.
Great Gate + Bell Star means hidden quarrels; the chance of being talked about behind your back and having words passed along is high.
Great Gate + Hindrance means drawn-out quarrels; one argument can drag on for years, so take the initiative to reconcile.

Great Gate in a Temple position and Fallen are very different. A person with Great Gate in the Life palace is best suited to earning a living by the mouth: debating, teaching, consulting, media, law, destiny reading and foreign languages are all professions that use the mouth, and by turning the gift of speech into a tool for earning money, quarrels will not waste your effort. The book describes Great Gate as “suspicious, learning widely but not finely, not well matched with people, with many quarrels and running about in toil”, meaning suspicious, learning a bit of everything without mastery, not getting along well with others, with plenty of gossip and a life of running around and hardship. So speaking carefully and acting carefully is Great Gate's first rule for getting through life.

Great Gate is in a Temple position at both Rabbit and Rooster (the Complete Book says Great Gate is “in a Temple position at the Rabbit and Rooster palaces, sharing with Strategist”). One view holds that when Great Gate is in a Temple or Prosperous position, most of the trouble is gone and turns into fluent speech and a very good gift of speech; most of the trouble is gone, not entirely gone. This person must take care not to contest everything, and to stop when things are good. Strategist and Great Gate at Rabbit in a Temple position (a Temple position means this star is strong here) make a fairly high pattern; at Rooster it is weaker.
Great Gate in the Spouse palace easily means a poor match; marry late and look for an older person, and with malefic stars you must be even more careful.
With Great Gate in the Career palace, your career does not leave the gift of speech and words.
With Great Gate in the Life palace, quarrels and gossip are the theme, and whether it is fortunate or unfortunate depends first on Temple or Fallen.

Great Gate belongs to Water and in the Northern Dipper governs darkness. It is also called the “dark star, star of gossip”, meaning the star that clouds matters and invites quarrels and gossip. It governs quarrels, gossip, debate and deep thinking. One view bluntly counts Great Gate as a malefic star, bringing troubles such as arguments, gossip and lawsuits, and whether it is in a Temple position (the star at full strength in this position) or Fallen (weak), gossip is plentiful and does not vanish because the star is bright.

When Great Gate is in a Temple or Prosperous position, the gift of speech and the power of discernment reach their peak, shining most in professions that need verbal expression, and gossip turns into eloquence and into a tool for making money.
When Great Gate is Fallen, the gift of speech drops and gossip in fact increases; you are easily misunderstood, your words need more care, and you should listen more and speak less.
Great Gate: the star of gossip and the gift of speech, good at debate, suited to lawyer, teacher and media work; in a Temple or Prosperous position the trouble lessens and turns into fluent speech.
The Emperor star meeting Greedy Wolf loves to play, has talent and is also a free spirit, and seeing Fire Star is even better, but guard against spending money on drink and women.
Save up young, harvest in middle age; the wealth fortune is bitter first and sweet after.
Integrity + Right Assistant means someone helps carry out your complex plans. It suits strategic planning, brand marketing and psychological warfare.
Integrity + Earth Robbery means complexity is robbed; love is easily snatched away and your career is cut in on by others.
Integrity + Earth Void means complexity turns to nothing; neither good nor bad things are certain to happen, and your fate has a feeling of “hanging in midair”.
Integrity + Heavenly Halberd means a female noble helper who resolves your complexity; in matters of the heart a female elder gives you wise advice.
Integrity + Heavenly Leader means a male noble helper who gets you through Integrity's “time of calamity”; when you meet a key setback in life, someone pulls you through.

Integrity + Left Assistant lets the complex energy of Integrity, the Prisoner star, be released in a reasonable way. It suits drawing on its strengths in power institutions, prosecution, legal affairs and strategy-leaning positions.

Integrity + Ram Blade is the classic malefic pattern “Integrity and Ram Blade”, meaning blood, official troubles and complicated love affairs. A person with this combination in the Friends palace easily meets a major pass before middle age.

Integrity + Ram Blade is the classic malefic pattern “Integrity and Ram Blade”, meaning blood, official troubles and complicated love affairs. A person with this combination in the Siblings palace easily meets a major pass before middle age.

Integrity + Ram Blade is the classic malefic pattern “Integrity and Ram Blade”, meaning blood, official troubles and complicated love affairs. A person with this combination in the Life palace easily meets a major pass before middle age.

Integrity + Ram Blade is the classic malefic pattern “Integrity and Ram Blade”, meaning blood, official troubles and complicated love affairs. A person with this combination in the Spouse palace easily meets a major pass before middle age.

Integrity + Ram Blade is the classic malefic pattern “Integrity and Ram Blade”, meaning blood, official troubles and complicated love affairs. A person with this combination in the Children palace easily meets a major pass before middle age.

Integrity + Ram Blade is the classic malefic pattern “Integrity and Ram Blade”, meaning blood, official troubles and complicated love affairs. A person with this combination in the Career palace easily meets a major pass before middle age.

Integrity + Ram Blade is the classic malefic pattern “Integrity and Ram Blade”, meaning blood, official troubles and complicated love affairs. A person with this combination in the Parents palace easily meets a major pass before middle age.

Integrity + Ram Blade is the classic malefic pattern “Integrity and Ram Blade”, meaning blood, official troubles and complicated love affairs. A person with this combination in the Property palace easily meets a major pass before middle age.

Integrity + Ram Blade is the classic malefic pattern “Integrity and Ram Blade”, meaning blood, official troubles and complicated love affairs. A person with this combination in the Health palace easily meets a major pass before middle age.

Integrity + Ram Blade is the classic malefic pattern “Integrity and Ram Blade”, meaning blood, official troubles and complicated love affairs. A person with this combination in the Fortune palace easily meets a major pass before middle age.

Integrity + Ram Blade is the classic malefic pattern “Integrity and Ram Blade”, meaning blood, official troubles and complicated love affairs. A person with this combination in the Wealth palace easily meets a major pass before middle age.

Integrity + Ram Blade is the classic malefic pattern “Integrity and Ram Blade”, meaning blood, official troubles and complicated love affairs. A person with this combination in the Travel palace easily meets a major pass before middle age.

Integrity + Literary Talent means intelligence and deep thought; you may achieve something distinctive in literature, design, branding and the arts. But guard against “being too clever for your own good”.

Integrity + Literary Arts: Literary Arts adds weight to Integrity's peach blossom, so your love life is complicated, and you should get to know the other person well before marriage. In career it favors public relations, diplomacy and artist management.

Integrity + Fire Star adds weight to the complexity of Integrity; love, official troubles and health (problems with blood) can all run into trouble. Be careful when driving and careful when signing contracts.
Integrity + Bell Star means hidden official troubles; it may be a legal dispute or an emotional tangle that only explodes many years later.
Integrity + Hindrance means complicated matters drag on longer; emotional entanglements, lawsuits and clan conflicts will all be prolonged.

With Integrity and Army Breaker both in the Spouse palace, one view judges it as either parting in life or parting in death, regardless of man or woman; the Complete Book also says “also harming and lacking harmony”, so living together is hard to keep harmonious.

With Integrity and Seven Killings both in the Life palace, a Prisoner star is paired with a general star, giving a fierce and decisive character that will not accept defeat and does not fear power. This pattern first depends on whether the stars are in Temple or Fallen positions, that is, strong or weak: the Complete Book states clearly that Integrity and Seven Killings in a Temple or Prosperous position are in fact people who accumulate a fortune, so it cannot simply be taken as an unlucky life.

With Integrity and Seven Killings in the Spouse palace, your spouse is upright and strong in temper. One view says plainly that this combination does not easily lead to separation the way Integrity and Greedy Wolf or Integrity and Army Breaker do, and seeing Integrity and Seven Killings in the Spouse palace actually counts as good, not as malefic. The Complete Book says Seven Killings in the Spouse palace “or marry late and avoid punishment”, meaning that marrying a little later avoids harm in the marriage, so marrying late suits you.

With Integrity and Seven Killings in the Career palace, your career relies on competition and decisive closing, and high-pressure fields such as the military and police, competitive contests and starting a business suit you best. The Complete Book says Seven Killings in a Temple or Prosperous position (strength) excels on a military-post path and is not suited to being a scholar; sharing the palace with Integrity, both reputation and standing rise. Only, when Integrity takes a military path, the stage of high rank and heavy power does not last long, so you must know to change direction in time.

With Integrity and Seven Killings in the Wealth palace, the Complete Book has the line “Seven Killings, together taking in the midst of bustle”, meaning money must come from busy places, won through competition, winning by the force of your charge and your decisiveness, not the kind that comes to you while lying idle. Volume three of the Complete Book says “Integrity and Seven Killings in a Temple or Prosperous position are in fact people who accumulate wealth”. Integrity and Seven Killings share a palace only at Ox and Goat, where Seven Killings is in a Temple position and Integrity is not Fallen, and the time of accumulation is considerably extended.

With Integrity in the Life palace or the Body palace (another key position in the chart), it already counts as the second peach blossom star (governing romantic bonds). Meeting Treasury, the storehouse star, turns the peach blossom force into the ability to nurture relationships between people. Treasury is also the storehouse of wealth, and in the Life palace it stands for a lifetime of ample food and clothing. When this pattern falls at the Dog palace and has benefic stars helping, the ancients described it as “gold belt at the waist, purple robe on the body”, meaning a high official with standing. You act with spirit without being rash, daring to decide while also knowing how to control risk.

Integrity in the Life palace is a secondary peach blossom, with talent and charm; how the peach blossom is read, and how heavy its good or bad is, depends on the stars sharing the palace and on Temple or Fallen positions.
With Integrity in the Career palace, the Complete Book says Integrity “in the Career palace has authority and power”.

With Integrity and Treasury both in the Life palace, a Prisoner star is paired with a wealth storehouse star. The book says Integrity is hard by nature and likes to contend, while Treasury is mild in heart, clever and widely learned. The Complete Book also says Treasury “can resolve all calamities”, but one view holds that Treasury standing alone is not read as resolving calamity, and only when it meets Three Terraces and Eight Seats is that discussed; here the latter reading is followed. When the two stars share the palace, the drive to win is reined in by calm, forming a character that is “hard outside, steady inside”, meaning it looks tough on the outside and is very steady within, good at overseeing the whole situation, and in an organization mostly holds a managerial role.
Integrity and Treasury sharing the palace look strong outside and calm inside, with very strong ability to oversee and manage.

With Integrity and Treasury in the Spouse palace, your spouse is dignified and calm, and knows how to run the household and handle money. Integrity standing alone in the Spouse palace would make marriage easily repeat, but with Treasury sharing the palace it turns into growing old together, and a person of upright nature in fact does not hurt the feelings. Treasury also stands for a cherished spouse and can help raise the standing of your partner. If Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void and Earth Robbery gather on it, you should marry a little later so that the feelings are not hurt. The original text of the chapter on wives and concubines in the Complete Book says of Treasury “meeting Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void or Earth Robbery, marrying late avoids punishment”, and of Integrity “Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star and Bell Star mean parting in life”; the original text does not say whether this is sharing the palace or shining from the trine palaces, and does not distinguish bright from dim, so you need to look at which star it is and how they meet.

With Integrity and Treasury in the Career palace, Integrity has Treasury sharing the palace, which stands for a dignified career and a comfortable, prosperous life; Treasury in the Career palace can do both civil and military posts, so it suits holding real power and sitting in an important management position. The spirit of Integrity paired with the calm of Treasury suits positions such as business management and overseeing administration. Meeting Earth Void and Earth Robbery, the reputation remains but the practical gains that reach your hands are only ordinary.

With Integrity and Treasury in the Wealth palace, Treasury is the storehouse of wealth, standing for a comfortable life, and is very good at holding on to large sums. The drive of Integrity paired with the conservatism of Treasury makes money management both attacking and defending, suiting overseeing finances and solid planning. Meeting Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void and Earth Robbery, money brings both success and failure, with clear ups and downs.

With Integrity and Minister both in the Life palace, a Prisoner star is paired with a seal star. The Complete Book says Minister has a kind, sincere appearance, a calm person, with no lack of food and clothing, and says Integrity is hard by nature, with a heart that rises and falls unsettled and likes to contend with others. So a person with this life pattern looks steady and keeps to the rules outside, but is hard by nature within, and easily contends with others when facing injustice.

With Integrity and Minister in the Spouse palace, your spouse is modest, gentle and kind, good-looking, and sweet and docile in temper. One view holds that meeting Minister is best when looking for a partner. The Complete Book says Integrity in the Spouse palace naturally carries a sign of remarriage, but with Minister sharing the palace and in a Temple position (strength) it does not reach the point of harming feelings. If it also meets Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void and Earth Robbery, feelings are still easily hurt and harmony is hard. The original text of the chapter on wives and concubines in the Complete Book says of Minister “adding Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void and Earth Robbery, punishment and harm”, and of Integrity “Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star and Bell Star mean parting in life”; the original text does not say whether this is sharing the palace or shining from the trine palaces, and does not distinguish bright from dim, so you need to look at which star it is and how they meet.

One view holds that meeting Minister is best when looking for a partner. The Complete Book says Integrity in the Spouse palace naturally carries a sign of remarriage, but with Minister sharing the palace and in a Temple position (strength) it does not reach the point of harming feelings. If it also meets Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void and Earth Robbery, feelings are still easily hurt and harmony is hard. For a woman's chart: a husband a little older suits you.

With Integrity and Minister in the Career palace, the Integrity entry in the Complete Book says “Minister and Treasury together, silk clothes, wealth and rank”, and the Minister entry says “with Integrity, a standing of authority and rank”.

With Integrity and Minister in the Wealth palace, the Complete Book says Minister in the Wealth palace stands for comfortable wealth, and sharing the palace with Integrity means “merchant trade creates wealth”, meaning money mostly comes from trade and business, not only from a fixed salary. Spending is moderate and not showy. If Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void and Earth Robbery also gather on it, the book says there will be both success and failure, wealth cannot be accumulated, and even large earnings cannot be kept.

A person with Integrity holding the Life palace has a fierce personality, passion, and talent in many fields; Integrity is called the “secondary peach blossom”, and Greedy Wolf is the true master of peach blossom. One saying holds that a person with Integrity narrows the eyes when smiling, with long narrow eyes and refined looks; these points compare physiognomy with the chart and need to be checked directly against the real person.

A person with Integrity holding the Life palace has a fierce personality, passion, and talent in many fields; Integrity is called the “secondary peach blossom”, and Greedy Wolf is the true master of peach blossom. One saying holds that a person with Integrity narrows the eyes when smiling, with long narrow eyes and refined looks; these points compare physiognomy with the chart and need to be checked directly against the real person. For a man's chart: there is another sign, that of carrying a smile before even speaking to a woman, which is the look of Integrity's secondary peach blossom showing on the face.

Integrity belongs to Fire and is the peach blossom star (governing romantic bonds) ranked second in the Northern Dipper. It is also called the Prisoner star, and also governs career, standing for talent, peach blossom, fierceness and passion. The old books write that a person with Integrity holding the Life palace has “eyes showing a spirited light” and a “stubborn, restless nature that likes to flare up and contend”, meaning bright, lively eyes, a hard nature that cannot sit still, a natural force to charge ahead, a liking to fight for the sake of a breath, talent shining outwards, and emotions with big swings too.

With Integrity in a Temple or Prosperous position (Tiger or Monkey palace) holding the Wealth palace, civil and military talents and the pull of peach blossom both turn into money; your social circle is your wealth circle, the more active you are the more money you have, and starting a personal brand or a creative venture suits you best.

When Integrity is in a Temple or Prosperous position, civil and military talents come fully into play, peach blossom is strong, the pull of socializing reaches its peak, and fortune in love and in social life is very good.

Integrity is a star that governs career. The old books say of Integrity in the Career palace: in a Temple position (strength) it is “a military post, with authority and rank”, meaning a military-post path such as the army or police can hold prominent power, only it does not easily last long. Sharing the palace with Seven Killings is “coming from a military background”, meaning starting a career by joining the army. In the three related palaces, seeing Emperor turns it into a civil post. Sharing the palace with Treasury and Minister is “silk clothes, wealth and rank”, meaning dressing with dignity and living in comfortable prosperity. Sharing it with Greedy Wolf means rising in bustling fields. One view also regards Integrity seated in the Life or Career palace as a “military officer sash”, meaning the road of leading troops into battle, often running off to distant regions.

When Integrity is Fallen in the Wealth palace or its trine and opposite palaces, peach blossom turns into bad peach blossom, money comes from untrustworthy people, and you easily meet romantic fraud or cheating in partnerships. You need to sharpen your ability to tell people apart, and in any important deal you must first check the other party's background clearly.

When Integrity is Fallen, talent and peach blossom fall, in love you easily meet people who are not genuine, the risk of official troubles rises, and you need to sharpen your ability to tell people apart.

With Integrity and Greedy Wolf both in the Life palace, two peach blossom stars (governing romantic bonds) stand shoulder to shoulder, the heaviest peach blossom combination in Zi Wei Dou Shu. The meaning of these two stars is this: Greedy Wolf is the number one peach blossom star, with drink, sex, wealth, temper and gambling all under its care, while Integrity is the second peach blossom star, taking the road of talent and charm. A person in this pattern has a striking appearance, strong affinity with the opposite sex, talent in many fields, and is also prone to being entangled in romance all life long.

With Integrity and Greedy Wolf in the Spouse palace, your spouse mostly has outstanding charm and strong affinity with the opposite sex, and you both have wide social circles, so the relationship is hard to keep quiet. The Complete Book says Greedy Wolf means “a bridegroom three times”, meaning the marriage does not easily hold firm in one go, and when Greedy Wolf is in a Temple position (strength) marrying a little later suits you even more. One view holds that seeing Integrity and Greedy Wolf (and Integrity and Army Breaker) in the Spouse palace, regardless of man or woman, means either parting in life or parting in death, and no exception has yet been seen. Marriage when young mostly cannot be kept, and being a little older and looking carefully before deciding is in fact steadier. If it also meets Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star and Bell Star, there is even more distance than closeness, and you may live in two places. In the chapter on wives and concubines in the Complete Book, both the Integrity and the Greedy Wolf entries have in the original text “Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star and Bell Star mean parting in life”, without saying whether it is sharing the palace or shining from the trine palaces, and without distinguishing bright from dim, so you need to look at which star it is and how they meet. When living together, talk first about boundaries and about keeping each other informed. When looking for a partner, it is not necessarily a good thing if the other person's Life palace is exactly the star of your Spouse palace: there is an example of a person with Minister in the Life palace and Integrity and Greedy Wolf in the Spouse palace, who chose a partner with exactly Integrity and Greedy Wolf in the Life palace, which counted as truly the end of the road. A person whose chart is already one of two marriages should in fact look for someone whose Eight Characters do not match their own before marrying.

With Integrity and Greedy Wolf in the Career palace, your career relies on connections and an eye for beauty, and bustling fields such as performance, fashion, beauty and food and hospitality suit you best. For this combination the Complete Book has only one line, “Greedy Wolf, power and rank in the midst of bustle”, meaning you gain advantage only where there are many people. Integrity and Greedy Wolf share a palace only at Snake and Pig, both Fallen positions (weak force), and the book also reminds you to act uprightly and keep moderation when holding power.

With Integrity and Greedy Wolf in the Wealth palace, money comes from relationships and bustling places, and goes into enjoyment, appearance and socializing, without sparing your hand. The trait of Greedy Wolf is to suddenly flourish and also suddenly break; money comes in strongly and also scatters fast. If you meet Fire Star, before thirty there is both success and failure, and after thirty you are in fact more likely to suddenly rise. In money matters you should set yourself a fixed set of rules for income and spending.

Integrity (the Prisoner star) and Army Breaker (the loss star) share a palace only at the Rabbit and Rooster palaces, where Army Breaker is Fallen (weak force). The old books say Army Breaker “if Fallen but adding malefic stars, breaks the ancestral home and leaves for a distant land”, meaning that Army Breaker Fallen with malefic stars added cannot keep the family estate and must leave home and go far away. A person with this life pattern mostly leaves home and becomes independent early, with very big ups and downs through life. When Seven Killings, Army Breaker and Greedy Wolf all shine on it at once (shining from other palaces), it stands for great change, a love of breaking new ground, and an unwillingness to settle for the ordinary.

Integrity: it carries secondary peach blossom as well as the air of a military officer, complete in both civil and military, with many talents; how the peach blossom is read depends on the combination and on strength or weakness.

Advice: after middle age, arrange something repetitive with a rhythm. Sitting meditation, tai chi, light yoga, gardening or baking are all fine, three times a week, to pull your mind out of calculation. More important is to make two or three female friends you can talk to honestly and meet them regularly to speak your heart; this is much more useful than carrying the load alone. Think through a risk to the point where it is acceptable and then stop, and do not keep imagining the worst case again and again.

Advice: buy an accident insurance policy; avoid overly strenuous exercise and high-risk activities; have regular health check-ups and do a routine blood test once, and if there is a problem, deal with it as the doctor advises. The essence of Army Breaker is “loss”, meaning drain, and it fears overwork most; the focus of caring for your health is regular hours, and do not stay up late and drain your vital energy.

Advice: when buying a home, give priority to three things. Light, whether it is near a park, and whether the neighbors are easy to live with; for your happiness these are much more practical than room for price rises. Save money by system and not by going without: each month move a fixed sum into a separate account, and spend the rest freely. In decoration, do not use cool tones and cold white light; warm light, warm colors and somewhat softer fabrics are your place, and do not skimp on this.

Advice: before age 35, try to have an experience of leaving your home region. A secondment, studying abroad or a transfer to another city are all fine, and this experience often decides how far you can go later. If you have already started a family, you can place the center of your career in a big city and put your home in a second- or third-tier city nearby. Once in the new place, do not just bury yourself in work; take the initiative to meet people, invite people to meals, and lay out a network of relationships there. Being alone out there is lonely after all, and what you lack is not ability but someone to receive you.

Advice: after thirty-five, set a goal that has nothing to do with enjoyment. Do something for the public good, train a hobby until it is presentable, or seriously build a career that belongs to you. The goal must be concrete enough to write down, with progress visible every month. When you feel lost inside, do not carry it alone; tell your worries to someone trustworthy, or start on a few concrete tasks, since this kind of feeling in you dissolves fastest through action.

Advice: do not rush to marry yourself off; the more you rush, the easier it is to get hurt. When looking for a partner, check three things: mature enough, able to bear responsibility, and not afraid of you being better than him. From the dating stage, state clearly the space and boundaries you need, for example the intensity of work, each person's own friends, and how money is handled; saying it clearly beforehand is better than slowly wearing it in after marriage. When you quarrel, speak about the matter, do not bring up old affairs, and do not judge the other person's character.

Advice: you do not need to join every social event of your relatives. Doing well the part you must do is enough, and missing a few is fine. Do not force yourself to be obedient; if you pretend for long, you will be the first who cannot bear it. With siblings, if you want to work together or put in money together, first write down the division of duties, the capital contributions and the rules for withdrawing. With the one or two people who are sincere with you, take the initiative to keep in touch and keep visiting.

Advice: there is no need to rush to start a family. Marrying a bit later, giving enough time to settle into each other, is in fact steadier. In daily life, discuss the boundaries between the two of you in advance: each person's career, each person's friends, how money is managed; saying it clearly beforehand is better than contesting who wins later. After a quarrel, remember to take the first step back: a soft word or cooking a meal both count. The two of you do not lack sparks; what is lacking is gentleness at the end.

Advice: whether you marry or not, keep your own income and account. Do not hang your whole livelihood on someone else. Set a monthly budget for socializing and appearance, and stop when it is exceeded. In investing, do not choose only what pays fast; hand part of it to a steadier form of management. Ups and downs at the start are normal, so do not change your whole path because of one loss.

Advice: whether you marry or not, keep an independent income and account for yourself. Your support must be held in your own hands. Male elders and colleagues with resources around you can be consulted when you need advice, but do not bet your whole road on one person. When choosing a partner, look at whether he can carry his work, and do not look only at title and show. When he is busy and cannot look after you, rather than waiting for him to come back, fill your own life with work; the more you have a center of your own, the steadier this relationship becomes.

Advice: whoever you are with, keep an independent account for yourself. Also keep a sum of money you can move at any time; it is the most practical support of your whole life. When a lot of money comes in, first move a fixed amount away and then spend. For large spending on the other person, past a certain figure, wait three days before deciding; anything involving loans, guarantees or buying a house together should be written clearly in black and white. Do not touch investments you do not understand; putting money into an industry you know is steadier.

Advice: whichever side you put your focus on, do not cut off this career road. Side jobs, skills and a second profession all count; first, you have your own money in hand, and second, do not let life shrink to circling inside the home. Each time you finish something, take the initiative to tell your superior clearly which part you did. If you plan to have children, discuss with your partner beforehand who will take on childcare and when to return to work, and it is best to write it down.

Advice: train yourself thoroughly in one thing. Take the initiative to ask for resources, a raise or a promotion. Before you speak up, write down three achievements of the past two years and state them in numbers; do not just say you have worked hard. Every two or three years, take the initiative to change position or take on a new project, since only when your position moves does your vision move. If you must take maternity leave, contact your superior once a month during the leave to discuss the team's progress, so that you are not pushed to the margins when you return.

Advice: train yourself thoroughly in one thing. They are still the same words, but change the timing and change the way you put them before saying them. Give opinions in private; in public, speak only about the matter and do not judge people. If you want to work for yourself, take the road of knowledge services, training, consulting, personal media or legal services, and build up clients through your reputation. Make more contact with senior people in the field who think highly of you; one introduction from them is more effective than ten applications from you. As for the income ceiling, raise it by relying on your personal brand.

Advice: from middle age on, take the initiative to arrange regular health check-ups for your parents. Go with them, and do not just transfer money. Make a fixed phone call every week, even if you only say three sentences; the frequency matters more than the content. Reconciling with your father is a lesson you must make up in this life, and it can start with a shared meal, listening to him tell stories of his youth, and it does not have to be that someone apologizes first.

Advice: from middle age on, take the initiative to arrange regular health check-ups for your parents. Go with them, and do not just transfer money; make a fixed phone call every week, even if you only say three sentences. With your parents-in-law, fulfilling the courtesies is enough, give care where it is needed, and closeness does not need to be forced, so that both sides stay at ease. Reconciling with your parents is a lesson you must make up after middle age, and it can start with a shared meal, listening to them tell stories of the old days.

Advice: from middle age on, take the initiative to arrange regular health check-ups for your parents. If any condition comes up, listen to the doctor and follow the doctor's instructions; do not look things up online yourself and label an illness. If you live far away, turn contact into a fixed habit: one call a week, even three minutes of talk is fine. With your parents-in-law, do not fall short where courtesy is needed, but keep your independence in feelings and do not force closeness, and in the long run you will fit together better. At work, you suit best a female boss who dares to reform; if you meet one, stay close to her.

Advice: take the initiative to seize chances of long-term business trips, transfers, or settling elsewhere. Do not begrudge moving your place of residence. When you go far, buy yourself an accident insurance package; you lose nothing. Do not drive at night, do not take up overly risky sports outdoors, and at construction sites, with machinery, knives and scissors, take one more look before you act; the most frightening thing is the gambler's thought “I will be fine”. When Power (taking authority) arrives, seize positions such as person in charge sent to another place or head of a branch.

When you go far, buy yourself an accident insurance package; you lose nothing. Do not drive at night, do not take up overly risky sports outdoors, and at construction sites, with machinery, knives and scissors, take one more look before you act; the most frightening thing is the gambler's thought “I will be fine”. When Prosperity (money coming in) arrives, the road to money in other places will open up clearly.

Advice: take the initiative to look for chances to appear in front of everyone. If you can go on stage, go on stage; if you can put your name on it, put your name on it, and do not let your credit sink into the collective. Find a partner at your side who specializes in checking details, hand the execution to them, and you take care of direction and outside dealings. Affinity with people is your strength, but when you need to state a view, do not be ambiguous; showing a little attitude now and then is what makes people take you seriously. Once a reputation collapses it takes many years to rebuild, so it is better to accept fewer jobs than to accept recklessly and then be unable to do them.

Advice: take the initiative to find a few trustworthy female friends and form an alliance. Do not copy the ways of male directors wholesale. With subordinates, lower your stance by half a step: be a little stricter about work and a little softer with people, because awe does not keep people, only sympathy does. For the rhythm of having children, wait until your career is a little steadier (after 30) before planning, which makes it more relaxed. If the company offers a chance of transfer, you should seize it, since it is mostly a step upwards.

Advice: take the initiative to put your child in an environment with people of different personalities. Sports teams, debate clubs, and activities that require both cooperating with others and competing with them are all good, letting the child early taste the link between effort and result. For things the child can do alone, do not rush to do them for the child, and when the child stumbles, do not rush to catch. Let the child eat a little blander food, have check-ups on schedule, and if the child feels unwell, take them to a doctor and follow the doctor.

Advice: take the initiative to accept your child's “difference”. Do not take the well-behaved child next door as a mold, since that would stifle your child's gift. Set few rules, and once set, hold to them, and leave the rest for the child to bump into. In a conflict, listen fully before you speak; the more you press your child, the more the child resists. If you plan to have a child, care for your body and daily life beforehand, and do not chase the clock. If the child has a physical problem, have regular check-ups and follow the doctor's instructions, without cross-checking and pinning it on any one organ.

Advice: take the initiative to “wean yourself”. Before thirty, support yourself; before thirty-five, arrange your own place to live; before forty, take on the duties the family needs carried. You can accept help from elders, but do not let them decide for you. From forty-five on, take the initiative to arrange for both of them to have a check-up once a year, and if a problem comes up, follow the doctor's words. When you work next to a strong superior, report progress clearly and directly once a task is done, and do not wait to be asked.

Advice: take the initiative to arrange safe adventures for your child. Traveling far alone, doing an internship elsewhere, joining an outdoor camp or a short study abroad are all fine. You do not need to truly make the child suffer, but you must let the child have seen the wide world, and then choose which road to take. When your child states a plan you do not agree with, do not rush to veto it; ask three questions: where does the money come from, what is the worst that could happen, and how long until you see results. If the child can answer, let the child try.

Advice: take the initiative to arrange safe adventures for your child. Outdoor camps, traveling far alone, an internship or a short study abroad elsewhere are all fine, letting the child broaden their horizons and then come back to choose a road. When your child states a plan you do not agree with, do not rush to veto it; ask where the money comes from, what is the worst that could happen, and how long until you see results; if the child can answer, let the child try. Your worries can be spoken, but after saying them, hand the right to decide back to the child.

Advice: take the initiative to keep up contact with your siblings. Do not wait for a problem before reaching out; ask after them at holidays, birthdays and on happy news, and only while the relationship is warm can you ask for favors.

Advice: take the initiative to let your child win an argument or two. This is not conceding defeat, but letting the child understand that reasoning works better than losing your temper. When the child asks why, do not find it a nuisance, and if you cannot answer, look it up together. Rules can be firm, but reasoning must leave room for flexibility; listen to what the child says before you speak.

Advice: take the initiative to ask the company for a raise. You are not used to speaking up, and it is very easy to end up long term with pay lower than your worth. Manage money by the steady road: fixed-term savings, stable funds and insurance, putting capital preservation first, and do not touch high-risk speculation. Turning your expertise into a service to take on extra work, for example consulting or side jobs, is the most suitable way for you to earn a little more. For the give and take of favors, set yourself a yearly ceiling, and when it is exceeded, say plainly that the budget is used up.

Advice: take the initiative to talk with your child about feelings and about the body. Also talk about moderation when with other people, and tell it using your own experience, which is far more effective than a single “no”. Support your child's artistic gifts as far as you can; pressing them down rigidly easily turns into an emotional problem. When preparing for pregnancy and during it, have prenatal check-ups on schedule, listen to the doctor, and do not scare yourself by relying on the chart. With your child, especially a daughter, always leave a road open for talking, and do not let the child suppress everything inside.

Advice: when buying a home, do not look only at whether the price rises. Look at whether the house can hold people: with one more room, parents can come to stay and friends can crash conveniently. Lean the decoration towards warmth, with wood, warm colors and natural materials; a minimalist style that is too cold will make you uncomfortable living there. Keep in the home a table where several people can sit, so friends and family can come and sit anytime. For real estate in your hometown, say early and clearly to the family who lives there and who manages it; with elders, remind them to have regular check-ups, and if they feel unwell, to see a doctor promptly.

Advice: when buying a home, do not look only at whether the price rises. Look at whether the house can hold people: with one more room, parents can come to stay and friends can crash conveniently. Lean the decoration towards warmth, with wood, warm colors and natural materials; a minimalist style that is too cold will make you uncomfortable living there. For real estate in your hometown, say early and clearly to the family who lives there and who manages it, and do not drag it out until a disagreement arises before discussing. With elders, remind them to have regular check-ups, and if they feel unwell, to see a doctor promptly.

Advice: when buying a home, do not seek to be done in one step. Give priority to locations and unit types that are easy to resell, and treat “can be swapped later” as a hard criterion. Do not spend too much money on decoration at once; first meet the need for comfortable living and leave the rest until the next home, and do not sign rental contracts that are too long either.

Advice: when buying a home, read the contract word by word before signing. Especially the clauses on floor area, handover time and compensation for breach; if you do not understand, pay someone to look. Take the initiative to keep up relations with neighbors, and tell them before construction begins, which can avoid most of the trouble. Do not be careless with electricity and fire in the home. The decoration can be bold and can have personality, but it must keep light and tidiness, because if you live long in a dark, heavy house your mood will be the first thing that cannot bear it.

Advice: when buying a home and decorating, do not chase trends. A style that is popular online is tiring after two years, a classic style suits you better, and money should go to things that last. When taking over the house and decorating, for the unseen places such as waterproofing and water pipes, put extra effort into acceptance inspection, and keep the contract and receipts. For anything involving a signature in house matters, even if people rush you, read the clauses clearly before putting pen to paper. Drink plenty of water every day, do not often hold in the need to go to the toilet, and each year do all the routine items of a health check-up.

Suggestion: start practicing asking for help from one small thing. When carrying things, ask someone to lend a hand, and when your heart is blocked, find someone to speak to. You do not need to be the problem solver every time. Following helping professions such as education, medicine, consulting and public welfare, you work with the most enthusiasm. Every week, set aside a stretch of time for yourself that no one can disturb. Live first as a person worth being taken care of, and only then go and take care of others; that is not selfishness, but a way of retreat you leave open for yourself.

Advice: from age forty on, get a full health check-up. Have a comprehensive exam plus the routine items for women, once a year without missing any. The Complete Book, volume two, in the Health palace section, under Seven Killings, says “Seven Killings: many calamities in childhood, and in adulthood often piles”, so do not skip the anorectal items either. If your body feels wrong, see a doctor early and follow the doctor's words, and do not bear it alone. Eat less spicy food, less tobacco and alcohol, and more vegetables. In exercise, add stretching, and do not train only heavy. When preparing for pregnancy and during it, take the initiative to slow your pace of life, and rest when you need to.

Advice: start with small things and put yourself first once. At this meal, order what you want to eat; this weekend, plan around where you want to go. When others ask you for something, ask yourself whether you still have the strength today, and if not, say so plainly. Each year buy yourself one slightly more expensive thing, just to make yourself happy. Twenty years from now, half of what you did for the family will be forgotten, but you will smile every time you pick up that item.

Advice: from the time your father turns fifty, take the initiative to care for his health. Pay special attention to the heart, blood pressure and eyes, steadily urge him to have check-ups, and if he feels unwell, go with him to see the doctor, and do not wait until something happens and then regret it. One more point: after marriage you will mostly, without realizing it, compare your father-in-law with your own father, and comparing back and forth you always feel something is missing. You must consciously remove this filter, and treat your father-in-law as an ordinary elder to live alongside, without expecting him to be like your father.

Advice: the two of you should set a rule. When you quarrel, speak only about what is in front of you, do not dig up old matters, and do not judge the other person's character. Whatever it is, say it clearly the same day, and do not hold it in and wait for the other to guess. Argue less over right and wrong, and even when opinions differ, let each other keep face. The two of you are the slow-burning type, so in the early stage spend a lot of time talking and building trust, and the deeper you talk the closer you grow. She helps you most in negotiation, relationships and information, and when you meet a situation you do not understand, listen to her first.

Advice: the two of you should agree that when you quarrel you speak only about what is in front of you. Also do not dig up old matters, and do not judge the other person's character. Whatever it is, say it clearly the same day, since if you hold it in alone the relationship wobbles along with it. Argue less over right and wrong, and even when opinions differ, let each other keep face. The two of you are the slow-burning type, so talk a lot, build trust, and the deeper you talk the closer you grow. He helps you most in negotiation, relationships and information, and when you meet a situation you do not understand, listen to him first.

Advice: keep your analytical ability while practicing softening the way you speak. For the same idea, affirm first and then raise the problem, and change “you should” to “I hope”, which makes a very different effect. In career you can confidently follow directions that live by the mouth and the mind, such as lawyer, teacher, media, consulting and foreign languages, where you have strong professional competitiveness. Before you speak, wrapping your words in a layer of gentleness is your most profitable investment.

Advice: before making a big decision, give yourself a day or two to calm down. Think through the worst case and only then start. When dealing with people, speak a little slower and soften your expression a little, and your ability to execute will turn into a pull that carries others along instead of pressing them down. Find yourself one more place where you do not need to be tense: when tired, admit being tired, and do not carry it alone to the end.

Advice: make saving compulsory. As soon as money lands in your account, take out a portion first, and what remains is what you may spend. Split investing into two parts: the capital-preservation part is not touched, and only the rest is taken to seek high returns, keeping the principal first. Before putting in large capital, spend a few days investigating the other party and the project clearly, and read every contract clause before signing. When young, first lay a solid professional foundation, and after middle age use steadier means to accumulate money.

Advice: make saving compulsory, taking out a portion as soon as money lands in your account. Split investing into two parts: the capital-preservation part is not touched, and only the rest is taken to seek high returns. Each month set aside five to ten percent of income as a reward for yourself, to buy something you want or go out for fun. For large household spending and for buying an investment property, take the initiative to call your husband in to decide together, so he feels involved; at the same time keep an account of your own, and this is better said clearly from the start.

Advice: first do one concrete thing. Look up the market rate of colleagues in the same field, raise your quote to the level you need, and stop taking jobs at favor prices. Invest by the steady road; things that can be held for the long term suit you, so do not touch high-risk short-term trading. When helping people, first set yourself a ceiling, and when it is exceeded, say so plainly. State premarital assets clearly, and within the marriage let each person keep separate books. This is in fact your own nature, and saying it straight leads to fewer conflicts.

Advice: first draw up a list of things you do not do. Which kinds of work you do not accept and which you do not help with; write them down, so that when someone asks you can say it. With siblings, do not make contact only when something comes up; in ordinary days a meal or a phone call, since affection comes from tending. If you want to cooperate, the division of duties must be written clearly in black and white, who manages the money and who decides; feelings are feelings and accounts are accounts.

Advice: first build one good home in a core location as your foundation. Then slowly add other conveniences; one home to live in plus one for investment is a fairly smooth structure. Before large deals, read the contract clauses word by word and do not mind the bother. For disputes about neighbors, property management and decoration, saying things clearly beforehand saves far more effort than arguing afterwards. Check the kitchen fumes and old electrical appliances in the home once a year.

Advice: first raise your own price. Compare it against the market rate in your field and recalculate once; raise it where it deserves raising. Many people like you are no less capable yet keep quoting low. Invest by the steady road; things that can be held for the long term suit you, so do not touch high-risk short-term trading. When helping friends, first set yourself a ceiling, and when it is exceeded, say so plainly. Each year set aside a day to work out income and spending clearly, and do not live by feeling.

Advice: first fix your daily routine. Each day try to go to bed at the same hour and get up at the same hour. Eat a little blander food, eat more vegetables, touch little spicy food, and do not drink coffee after the afternoon. Choose exercise with a rhythm: brisk walking, light jogging, swimming, cycling, three times a week for half an hour each, which is the best way to burn off some of the fire in you. Have a routine check-up once a year, and record changes in sleep, mood and periods on your phone to show the doctor at the exam; for palpitations, heavy sweating or erratic weight swings, follow the doctor's suggestion and get checked, and do not look it up online and scare yourself.

Advice: first fix your daily routine. Sleep time and meal time matter more than what you eat. Eat on time and eat less spicy food. For exercise, choose something with a feeling of novelty; wall climbing, combat sports and martial arts are all fine, and the key is that you can keep it up; wear protective gear properly, and do not push on while injured. Have a regular check-up every year; if your body has a problem, see a doctor in time, follow the doctor's words, and do not bear it alone.

Advice: first steady your own emotions. This is the most practical protection you can give your child: when you feel bad, find someone your own age to talk to, and do not treat your child as your listener. When the child has not done well, allow the child not to have done well, and do not rush to lecture. Take your child to do a few useless things, such as kicking a ball, running around, or spacing out, since childhood is born to be wasted. For the body, take the child for check-ups on schedule, and when the child feels unwell, listen to the doctor. The child does not need a perfect mother; the child needs a genuine mother who also knows how to be tired.

Advice: first reduce the information coming to you. Look less at parenting sites, set do-not-disturb on the parents' group, and do not ask around about other people's children's progress. Trust your own eyes and your child's pace; when the child learns to walk and talk, there is no need to compare with others. Manage principles, not details: safety, honesty and attitude towards others are to be held firmly, and the rest is for the child to try. When panic rises inside you, put your phone down and play with your child for twenty minutes, and mostly you will be fine.

Advice: when you go out, choose work with a challenge. Starting a business, expanding a market, or being sent elsewhere to do a project are all fine; do not choose the kind of job that only changes your office seat, which will drain your strength. When you are out and have been drinking, do not touch a car, and when you meet a dispute, step away first and discuss it later. On arriving in a new place, first spend three months seriously making a few local friends, and only then is your road steady.

Advice: when you go out, seriously tend your relationships in far-off places. A few friends you can invite to a meal, and one person you can call in the middle of the night, matter more than earning a bit more money. If you marry far away, keep your own career, circle and account, and you do not need to follow your husband's family in everything; if you are truly being pressed down, say so plainly, since gritting your teeth means you are the first one hurt. When you are out and have been drinking, do not touch a car, and when you meet a dispute, step away.

Advice: when you go on business trips and travel alone, set a few hard rules. Do not go to nightlife spots, drink little, refuse private invitations from strange men, and do not meet privately people you know only from the internet. Keep your documents and valuables yourself, send a copy of your itinerary to your family, and choose lodging in a safe area. If you are already married, try not to live apart from your husband for the long term; if it truly cannot be avoided, say so beforehand and agree on how often you will come home.

Advice: when you go on business trips, set a few hard rules. In the evenings try not to go to drinking parties, do not drive after drinking, and refuse private invitations from the opposite sex or bring along extra colleagues. Guard your wallet as well: casinos, nightlife spots and luxury goods are the three things most likely to ruin matters in far places. Keep your documents and itinerary safe and send a copy to your family. Money earned outside is favor money; remember who has helped you and repay them afterwards, which is far more effective than drinking three more cups.

Advice: when you go out, put your own affairs first. Only when home, work and health are stable should you think of helping anyone. When others ask you for something, do not rush to agree; say “let me think and I will reply”, and most matters will no longer need your worry by the next day. On arriving in a new place, take the initiative to get to know a few older colleagues, who can help you a great deal. For big decisions in far places, wait two weeks before settling, and do not agree on the spot.

Advice: distinguish clearly between giving advice and bearing the consequences. When others ask you, laying out the pros and cons is enough; do not decide for them, much less act for them, because only a road they choose themselves is one they can bear. In friendships, better few and deep. Some people look close but are not truly of one heart, so be careful with deep friendship. Also, you can ask others for help too. You have helped so many people, and letting them repay you once makes the relationship equal.

Advice: do not pin the label of “complicated love life” on yourself. Rather than suppressing it, put that energy into a field that always gives you a feeling of freshness: entertainment, fashion, media and sales, places that cannot hold boredom, which suit you very well. In love, set yourself a period of observation; a racing heart is a racing heart, but first see whether this person can get through the next morning's breakfast with you. If you truly meet someone who wins you over completely, you are in fact more loyal than anyone.

Advice: do not force yourself into circles whose values differ from yours just to fit in. Save that energy for the few people who accept the way you manage things. The few friends who have walked through some big upheavals with you are worth keeping up actively: meet regularly, and truly be there when something happens. For friendships with an element of cooperation, state money and the division of duties clearly beforehand, so the feelings do not easily break within them.

Advice: do not go into partnerships on a verbal “being loyal is enough” basis. For you the chance of falling out is very high. If you want to work together, go project by project, write the contract in detail, and state clearly beforehand how the accounts are split and how to withdraw, ideally with a third party both recognize to oversee the books.

Advice: do not go into partnerships on a verbal “being loyal is enough” basis. For you the chance of falling out is very high. If you want to work together, go project by project, write the contract in detail, and state clearly beforehand how the accounts are split and how to withdraw, ideally with a third party both recognize to oversee the books. When Prosperity (money coming in) arrives, partnering with them is in fact likely to make money.

Advice: do not force yourself to become the kind of person who hangs feelings on the tongue. For words you are not good at saying, use actions: remember birthdays, bring a small gift at holidays, and when something comes up, ask first. For partnerships, accounts and shares, speak beforehand, and settle even how to withdraw from the start; your frankness combined with clear rules is what keeps you from being seen as heartless.

Advice: do not force yourself into circles you do not like. Put your effort into two or three friends who are as independent and practical as you; women of the entrepreneur type or the professional type often suit you best. In partnerships, the contract and the withdrawal mechanism must be written beforehand, and as for acting as guarantor for others, try not to get involved, because the one who suffers the loss is mostly you.

Advice: do not look only at whether your child performs well. Ask one more question, “which one do you want”. When the child says anything is fine, or says both are fine, that is exactly the time to ask most persistently. Hand your child some matters they can truly decide for themselves, such as which class to register for, how to arrange the weekend, or how to set up the room, and even if they choose wrong, let them sort it out once on their own. If your child suddenly goes quiet at puberty, do not rush to say the child is unreasonable; sit down and listen to everything the child has to say first.

Suggestion: do not just bury yourself in work. Doing your profession well is only half; the other half is letting the people who need to know know what you are doing, reporting progress regularly, and finding a senior person to act as your guide. If you take the road of state employment, a steady, solid path suits you better than risky entrepreneurship. Do not be afraid of changing direction either; you can handle both civil and military posts, and your road is wider than you think.

Advice: do not stage dramas in your own heart. When doubt arises, ask a direct question, which is far better than thinking for three days. When choosing a partner, do not look at whether they know how to coax you; replying to messages on time and doing what they promise matter much more than romance. At work you do not need to rush for the position in front of the stage; first forge solid ability in producing plans and setting direction. Each day keep a stretch of time free of thinking, doing a few things with your hands, to pull your attention from your head back to your hands.
Advice: do not wear yourself out in an office position. Head for positions with real power and hard targets. Do not always treat rivals as enemies either; where cooperation is possible, cooperate.

Advice: do not shy away from appearing in front of everyone; if you can go on stage, go on stage, and if you can put your name on it, put your name on it. Have beside you a partner who specializes in checking details, hand the execution to them, and you take care only of direction and outside dealings. Affinity with people is a strength, but when you need to state a view, you must state it; being the nice person forever means no one truly takes you seriously. Most important is that your words and deeds are consistent; once a reputation collapses it takes many years to rebuild, so it is better to accept fewer jobs than to say yes and then be unable to do them.

Advice: do not rush to settle marriage while young. First keep your own rhythm steady. If both of you love freedom, one of you must take care of keeping life stable: who manages money and who manages the house should be stated clearly beforehand. When living together, use the method of “trying someone else” less to solve problems, and when there is a conflict, speak about it clearly the same day. Passion alone cannot hold up for long, so put your plans for a long life together on the table and discuss them.

Advice: do not rush to settle down. Live together a while longer and see clearly whether he can bear responsibility. When Sun is Fallen (weak force), it suits starting a family a bit later; for a woman's chart with the combination of Great Gate and Sun where Sun is Fallen, when choosing a partner you can look for someone seven or more years older than you, or someone who has been divorced. When living together, leave room for each other, and do not use whether he is at home to measure whether he loves you, but state clearly the requests you need to make: each week set aside a stretch of time that belongs only to the two of you. This is the base brought by your birth year; which Decade and which year it gets activated must be read further through the periods of fortune.

Advice: do not rush to settle things for life. First see how this person treats family and how they treat money; these two places show the roots most clearly. When living together you can be a little more proactive: you are used to keeping up appearances, and the other person usually cannot read what you are thinking, so saying plainly what you want is much more useful than waiting for him to guess. If you truly meet a relationship that puts you in a difficult spot, state your boundaries clearly and widen the distance, and do not fear being called heartless.

Advice: do not rush to map out a famous road for your child. Let the child choose, and you take care of the backing. In front of outsiders, do not compare your child with others, and at home say less of the kind of line about having to bring glory to the family. From small, help your child keep good eye habits, stay up less late, look at screens less for long, and have vision checked when needed.

Advice: do not rush to open your own company. First build a professional reputation on a good platform, where income rises faster; if you truly want to be independent, you must find a partner who does practical work to make up for the execution side. Wide interests are a good thing, but you must pick one direction and dig in, and do not know a little of everything and master nothing. For important matters, once your mind is made up, do not keep changing it back and forth, so that others dare to hand work to you.

Advice: do not think that career and marriage are a choice of one or the other. That is not a price fixed in the chart, but a matter of how you arrange things. At work, the loss you most easily suffer is just burying yourself in work; remember to let the people who need to know know your results, report regularly, and take the initiative to win projects. In the team your attitude is a bit cool, so each week you can take the initiative to invite a colleague to a meal, since relationships come from chatting.

Advice: do not take the feeling of novelty as the standard for whether love is good. It is normal for passion to settle, and afterwards you rely on the skill of living together. Set a few fixed things you must do, for example one evening each week just for each other, and one trip together each year. If both of you love freedom, one of you must take the initiative to carry the stability, and who carries it should be stated clearly beforehand. If you truly must live apart in two places, settle how often you will meet before you go.

Advice: do not set your standards too high. While holding firm to your own principles, show a little more gentleness to those who truly care about you. In career you can confidently try many directions, with no need to lock into one road early. In love there is no need to rush; for someone like you, meeting the right person a little later is in fact steadier, and once you truly meet, stating your boundaries and limits clearly works better than anything else.

Advice: do not bring personal emotions into working relationships. Keep words that are hard to hear in your heart for a day before saying them. You may work for yourself, but it is best to find a calm person to manage operations and accounts, and you take care only of creativity and outside dealings. In ordinary days watch for two kinds of people: those who see your talent and are willing to give you a chance, and those who, when you get into trouble, are willing to stand up and speak for you and smooth things over for you; both kinds are worth keeping up with for the long term. Reputation matters more than a momentary win or loss, and love affairs should not be brought into the company at all.

Advice: do not put all your money into one big house. Before marriage, when buying a home, give priority to a smaller unit that is easy to sell. When buying a home with your husband, state clearly beforehand the share of capital contributed and whose name is on the documents; black and white is more reassuring than spoken words. Divide up decoration work: whoever cares about it decides, and do not let the two of you tug over every detail. Most important is to keep a space of your own, whether a reading room, a balcony or a small corner; without this place, your thoughts will be drowned by household chores and the voices of the family.

Advice: do not put all your money into one big house beyond your needs. Keep a portion where you can use it at any time. When choosing a home, give priority to units that are easy to sell, in familiar locations, of a common type that resells quickly, which matters more than being done in one step. For decoration choose things that can be changed: furniture that can be moved and partitions that can be removed, and do not seal everything shut. If you have moved too often in the past two years, stay put for three years before considering a change, since when a person is settled first, matters get arranged smoothly.

Advice: do not expect to persuade your parents to understand your way of life. Put your effort where they can accept it: regularly go home for meals, and each year go with them for a health check-up. When you argue, pause for half a minute first; what they need is usually not for you to obey, but confirmation that you are living steadily. At work, get closer to calm superiors, and people from traditional industries, banking and state backgrounds are the most likely to take a liking to you.

Advice: do not expect to stand firm by relying on inheritance. If you build your own estate outside, both generations are in fact at ease. Show filial care in the way you are good at: help your parents arrange health check-ups, insurance and care in old age, which is more practical than fine words. When you are at odds with your mother, first do not argue over right and wrong; waiting a day and then speaking again usually settles it. After marriage, with your parents-in-law, fulfilling the courtesies is enough, and keeping a little distance is how you will be comfortable.

Advice: do not expect to stand firm by relying on inheritance. If you build your own estate outside, both generations are in fact at ease. Show filial care in the way you are good at: arrange health check-ups for your parents, buy insurance, and find good medical resources, which is more practical than fine words; when you have time, call more often, even if only for three sentences. At work you suit best superiors who do real work; if you meet a leader who goes by feeling, report progress often and argue over right and wrong little.

Advice: do not wait for your parents to speak up. From middle age on, take the initiative to arrange regular health check-ups for them, and if any condition comes up, listen to the doctor and follow the doctor's instructions; do not look things up online and label an illness. If you live far away, turn contact into a fixed habit: one call a week, even three minutes of talk is fine. With your father, you do not necessarily have to talk everything through; doing a few concrete things together, fixing something, or going with him to the hospital is more useful than heart-to-heart talks.

Advice: do not fight your own desires head-on.
