The “Complete Book”, volume two, under the Health palace, the Minister entry, says “Minister brings few misfortunes, with a sallow, puffy complexion and ailments of qi and blood”; serious illness is rare, but your complexion, skin, and qi and blood need watching, plus cervical vertebrae and lower back damaged by long sitting, so mention these to the doctor when you are examined; if your body feels unwell, see a doctor promptly and follow the doctor's advice, and do not bear it alone and let it drag on. In daily life, drink plenty of water, eat a little plainer, and go easy on oil, salt and spice. After sitting for an hour, stand up and move for five minutes, stretch the neck, shoulders, back and waist, and add some gentle aerobic exercise such as brisk walking and swimming. For what you suppress in your heart, find someone to talk to, and when needed find a professional to talk with; this works better for you than eating anything.

My advice: have regular health check-ups every year. The “Complete Book”, volume two, under the Health palace, the Minister entry, says “Minister brings few misfortunes, with a sallow, puffy complexion and ailments of qi and blood”; serious illness is rare, but your complexion, skin, and qi and blood need watching, and do not skip the examinations related to women; if your body feels unwell, see a doctor promptly and follow the doctor's advice. In daily life, drink plenty of water, eat plain food, and go easy on salt and spice; after sitting for an hour, stand up and move for five minutes, stretch the neck, shoulders, back and waist, and add some gentle aerobic exercise such as brisk walking and swimming. Most important is not to carry it all alone: during pregnancy and the postpartum month, discuss in advance with your family how to divide housework and work; if your mood keeps sinking, take the initiative to ask your family and professionals for help.

My advice: have regular health check-ups every year. Do not skip the full check-up or the routine examinations for women, and if you feel unwell, see a doctor and follow the doctor's orders. Eat a little plainer, eat more vegetables, and go easy on spicy food and alcohol. Find a form of exercise that lets you vent your fire, such as running, dancing or boxing, three times a week. If your emotions swing sharply before and after pregnancy, tell your family in advance and ask them to lend a hand; seeking professional help when needed is also perfectly normal. If surgery has to be arranged, discuss the timing and preparation clearly with your treating doctor beforehand.

My advice: have regular health check-ups every year. Let the doctor arrange which items to check; if you feel unwell, see a doctor and follow the doctor's orders, and do not bear it alone, nor look things up online and frighten yourself. Eat a little plainer, eat more vegetables, and go easy on spicy food and alcohol. Find a form of exercise that lets you vent your fire, such as running, boxing or dancing, three times a week, which works better than any tonic food. If you truly have to have surgery, discuss the timing and preparation clearly with your treating doctor beforehand.

My advice: each year, push yourself to try one or two uncertain things. Start with small sums you can afford to lose, where losing does not eat into your capital and winning supplies a bit of the drive you lack most. You do not like to take the initiative in befriending new people, so widen your circle through work, and a few new acquaintances a year are enough. When the pressure is heavy, do not think only of reinforcing your defences; first ask yourself one question: how bad can the worst case get? If you can answer it, you will dare to move.

My advice: at least once a year, talk plainly with your superior about a promotion or a raise. List what you accomplished during the year as concrete figures for him to see. When choosing work, give priority to the platform; for you, whether the platform is high or low matters more than an individual's head-down hard work. If you really start a business, find someone with ambition and resources to lead the big direction while you take care of internal matters and execution, with the division of work written down clearly. Pay a lot of attention to your direct superior and to the elders with a voice in the industry; your benefactors are the kind who guide you over the long term.

My advice: every time you earn a large sum, take out the principal first. Put it into an account that is hard to touch. Set a maximum monthly spending limit for yourself and stop when it is exceeded; gambling-like speculation and large outlays in love are the two biggest holes you have. For investing, choose projects with short cycles and within reach of your own connections, and do not pour money into something that has to be left for ten years. When young, do not bet the whole family fortune at once; keep your capital, and you will be able to catch the middle-age wave.

My advice: right now, choose one thing you have already done for three years or more. Dig in for another three years, and do not turn back every time you see a new direction. Set yourself a cooling-off period: when you want to change direction, write it down first and leave it for a month to see whether you still want to change. As for position, there is no need to force yourself to be the head; being the one who is asked again and again is more at ease.

My advice: when you employ people, set the rules first. Hold the authority over money and over signatures in your own hands, and reconcile the accounts regularly. For any guarantee, loan, or stepping in to settle someone else's trouble, sleep on it a night before answering. If a circle does not suit you, there is no need to force yourself to fit in; save the energy for the right people. Since you have few friends, you must be all the more proactive in arranging to meet and in asking how they have been lately, because relationships come from going back and forth.

My advice: when you employ people, set the rules first. Hold the authority over money and over signatures in your own hands, reconcile the accounts regularly, and settle accounts clearly even with your own siblings. For any guarantee, loan, or stepping in to settle someone else's trouble, sleep on it a night before answering; the next day you will most likely judge differently. With the few people who are sincere with you, take the initiative to arrange meetings and to keep in touch; your friends are few to begin with, and each of them deserves your effort.

My suggestion: let a system manage money for you. Pay in fully to the housing fund, have the mortgage deducted monthly, and transfer a fixed sum into your home-purchase account each month, which works better than forcing yourself to hold back. Do not borrow right up to the limit; leave enough money for yourself to live comfortably, or you may be unable to hold out midway. For the furnishings, do not copy the cold, hard grey-and-white style; rugs, cushions, warm lighting, fragrance and other small items that do not catch the eye matter a lot to you, so do not skimp on what is worth spending.

My advice: leave the old path that your family already has. Charging out into the world with a trade is the direction in which you can get through. After breaking down the old, force yourself to build the new, and do not break things down and then leave: choose a field, stay in it for a full three years, and make it take shape. Deciding by intuition is fine, but for big matters sleep on it before settling, adding a layer of cushion to your impulses.

My advice: practise a new habit: after listening, do not solve things for the other person. Very often people only need someone to listen to them seriously, not an answer. If you really want to help, ask one question: what do you plan to do? and hand the decision back to her. In making friends, prefer few but deep. Also, you may ask others for help; you have helped so many people, so let them repay you once, and only then will the relationship be on an equal footing.

My advice: practise a gentle way of refusing. There is no need to throw away your dignity; one sentence, “I am not in good shape today, another day I will listen to you,” is enough. When listening to friends pour out their troubles, set a time limit for yourself and stop after one hour. For anything involving loans, guarantees or asking favours through connections, wait a night before answering. To widen your circle, start from your own interests and specialty: exhibitions, book clubs and industry gatherings; the people you meet in these places walk the same path as you.

My advice: practise two things. One is to state your own needs, what you want and what you will not accept, saying it clearly rather than enduring it; the other is to draw yourself a boundary, so that you know clearly in your heart how far you will help with other people's affairs. At work, administration, legal affairs, human resources and assistant roles are where you shine most, but do not stop at doing only execution; once a year, take the initiative to put your own ideas to your superior. The person to look for is the one who sees what you put in; someone who takes your goodness for granted is not worth wearing yourself out for.

My advice: before you marry, have one serious talk with your parents. It is not about demanding an apology from anyone, but about saying everything in your heart once. In daily conversation, ask more and comment less, and even if their reasoning is outdated, listen to all of it first. When you are with your parents-in-law, analyse less and listen more; your analysis sounds like nitpicking in the ears of older people, so save your sharp eloquence for work. When you have something to say, choose a quiet moment to say it, and once this matter is said, turn the page.

My advice: when you marry and buy a home, take part in choosing it yourself. You are especially sensitive to whether a house pleases your eye, and if others choose for you, you will always feel ill at ease living there. Do not chase trends in the decoration; spend the money on things that last. For the parts you cannot see, such as waterproofing and water pipes, put in extra effort at the acceptance inspection, and keep the contract, receipts and warranty slips. For anything about the home that involves signing and transferring ownership, read the terms clearly before putting pen to paper; no matter who hurries you, this one day cannot be skipped.

My advice: before you marry, find a way to get yourself a small home. Even if it is small, it is your support. For the decoration, first settle the budget; half of what looks good in a show flat will go unused once it enters real life. Be careful with fire and electricity, and check the sockets, gas and range hood regularly. Each week keep one fixed meal for family only; if a household is left with only gatherings, the cracks in affection grow bit by bit, and by the time you notice, it is too late.

My advice: marry a little later. There is no need to fix an age limit on yourself; before settling down, first understand how the other person spends money and how they live their days, which is more useful than sweet words. You show love through actions, so remember to let the other person know what you are doing, or he will only see that you are capable and will not see that you care.

My advice: find a fixed outlet for what is in your heart. Write it out, draw it, or go out for a walk alone, or read a few thick books, at least once a week, and do not wait until you are full of suppression and then burst out. When you feel unwell, find someone who will speak honestly and tell them about it, and after telling you will feel half lighter. Keep one thing in hand that you are working on, and do not let yourself be idle for too long. If you feel low for several weeks in a row, sleep poorly and have no energy, talking with a professional is a perfectly normal choice, far better than pushing through on your own.

My advice: find a fixed outlet for the fire in your heart. Write it out, draw it or run it off, at least once a week, and do not wait until you are full of suppression and then burst out. When you feel unwell, find someone who will speak honestly and tell them about it, and after telling you will feel half lighter. Do not let yourself be idle for too long either; keep one thing in hand that you are working on. If you feel low for several weeks in a row, sleep poorly and have no energy, find a professional to talk with, which works better than pushing through on your own.

My advice: set a time limit on thinking. It is not about not thinking, but about stopping when the time is up and acting when it is good enough. From middle age you can try sitting meditation, mindfulness, or the habit of writing, steering the momentum of over-analysis toward something that produces results. For what you suppress in your heart, find someone to speak with regularly; just speaking it out already makes you half lighter. Each day leave half an hour to think about nothing at all, and let the mind go empty for a while with a walk or music.

My advice: leave a buffer zone for your emotions. Do not decide while angry, and do not rush to reply; wait a night and then discuss, which will block most of your troubles. Using this surge of energy on your main work, doing things that need spirit and creativity, is far more beneficial than confronting other people. In dealing with people, take the initiative to stay out of gossip between men and women; how close you get to someone and how far, draw the line in your heart first.

My advice: set an alarm for your thinking. If twenty minutes pass without a conclusion, do something else first, and thinking again the next day usually clears it up. When you have a misunderstanding with someone, do not guess on your own; asking one direct question saves you three days. In making friends, choose people who can have deep talks with you, because you cannot bear relationships that float on the surface. Most important: this mouth of yours can help you earn money and win back what is right, and it can also, in three seconds, ruin the relationship you value most; when words reach your mouth, think one step further.

My advice: build yourself a quick judgement table. Choose five key criteria, and when they all fit, act without further hesitation. For investing, choose directions you have studied and understood; copyright, intellectual property, education and other fields that live on information suit you best, so do not chase the crowd. When discussing money at home, mind your manner; your analysis often sounds like questioning to your other half, so say “let's look at it together” first, and then lay out your reasoning. Most important is still building a reputation and avoiding disputes; when these two are done well, your money will be steady.

My advice: set yourself a rule. Before you want to tear something down, write out what you will build in its place; if you cannot write it, do not move. From middle age, choose one field to dig deep into; even a small stall, if made deep and thorough, gives your heart a place to rest. Each day leave half an hour to do nothing, without looking at your phone or thinking about plans, and let the mind go empty for a while.

My advice: set yourself a rule. Before you want to tear something down, write out what you will build in its place; if you cannot write it, do not move. In youth you broke down many old things; by middle age you should try building once, not rebuilding the past but building something new that belongs only to you. Each day leave half an hour to do nothing, and let the mind go empty for a while.

My advice: set three lines for yourself. In other people's romantic disputes, only listen and do not comment, and do not act as a go-between; for money among friends, either give it or do not lend it; and stay out of anything in a grey area altogether. When you hear a rumour about someone, verify it first and then decide whether to get involved. Better to have a slightly smaller circle than to keep a crowd of people who will cause you trouble for the sake of liveliness.

My advice: set yourself a waiting period. Put what you want to buy on a list first, and decide only after three full days, by which time you will mostly no longer want it. Make a list of monthly subscriptions and cancel at once any you do not use. Limit your investment directions to two or three, do not touch what you do not understand, and keep enough cash in hand. Keeping an account of your capital is your strength; add one more thing: on payday each month, automatically transfer a sum to save first, and what remains is what you may spend.

My advice: set yourself a rule. Act when you have thought it through to seven-tenths, and fix the remaining three-tenths as you go. For important decisions, find someone who works reliably to help you settle them, and do not go around in circles alone in your head. At work, pick one direction and stay put for three to five years, first making one thing so good that others cannot overlook you, and only then touch something new. When dealing with people, state clearly what you have decided and let people guess less.

My advice: set yourself a few concrete goals and completion dates. Do not just wait for opportunity to come to your door. You take on many cooperative tasks, so try to team up with people who have drive, and let them lead you forward. When an occasion calls for competing, think clearly about what you want and then put it into words, even if you say only one sentence at a time. For things that need to be decided on the spot, list the options and your final limits in advance, and do not let others rush you into deciding.

My advice: set yourself a few lines. In other people's romantic disputes, only listen and do not comment, and do not act as a go-between; in dealings with friends of the opposite sex and colleagues, keep to public settings and do not meet alone late at night; for money among friends, either give it or do not lend it. When you hear a rumour about someone, verify it first and then decide whether to get involved. Better to have a slightly smaller circle than to keep people who will cause you trouble.

My advice: find yourself one or two hobbies that have nothing to do with money. Hiking, fishing, calligraphy or collecting are all fine; something whose return cannot be calculated is exactly what best relieves your anxiety. Each day leave half an hour without looking at your phone or thinking about work; the kind of relaxation that gets the body moving works better for you.

My advice: find yourself a source of support that does not depend on others nodding. Make a fixed habit of reading a little, writing a little, painting or practising a craft, or set aside a stretch of quiet solitude each week, so that you can be at ease alone. From middle age, calming activities such as sitting meditation and yoga, or finding a professional to talk with about what is in your heart, are all worth trying. You can enjoy applause, but do not treat it as the only reason to live; before and after perimenopause, this dependence will become especially heavy.

My advice: keep a corner for yourself where you can be alone. Even if it is only a desk. This is not distrust of your other half, but a person like you needs a quiet place to think things through. For big matters like buying a home or transferring ownership, first ask an expert to go through the contract clause by clause and make sure the ownership is clearly written. When quarrelling at home, each of you spend five minutes alone and then talk.

My advice: keep for yourself one line that you do not yield on for anyone else. Think clearly beforehand which matters can be discussed and which cannot, and when you say no there is no need to explain much. In your career do not wait for people to push you; each year set one concrete goal, write it down, and then tell someone who will press you on it. Choose a trade you can practise for the long term and go deep into it, and in your peaceful days keep a little upward drive, so that your road does not narrow the further you go.

My advice: give yourself a 24-hour cooling-off time. Put what you want to buy in the shopping cart first, and decide after a day. As soon as you receive your salary, take out a sum and transfer it to an account that money goes into but does not come out of; do not wait until you have spare money to save. For the family finances, rather than forcing a joint account, it is better for each to manage what they earn, and for large shared expenses to be discussed clearly and written down. Invest only in fields you know, and do not add capital when prices are at a peak.

My advice: for matters you keep turning over and over, set a time limit. When it passes, land the plane: either ask directly to get it clear, or let it go completely, and do not nurse it in your heart. The most important lesson in this life is to tell which matters are worth calculating over and which are not: before losing your temper, ask yourself whether this will still matter a year from now. For relationships in a grey area, a lawsuit that can go unfiled, or money of unclear origin, avoid them if you can.

My advice: set a monthly ceiling on spending to keep up appearances, and stop when it is exceeded. When discussing cooperation, first inquire about the other side's reputation and only then talk money, and better to take fewer orders. Hand part of your money to someone steadier or to a more conservative method to manage, and do not pour everything into the fast project you favour. Ups and downs in the early years are normal, so do not change your whole road because of losing once or twice.

My advice: hold the tempo yourself. When it is time to step onto the field, give it your all, and when tired, withdraw for a while on your own initiative: you decide to withdraw, rather than being chased off. In the low period, do not force yourself to socialise; turn off your phone and find something to do where no one has to see you, such as fishing, walking a mountain path or growing something; from middle age this outlet matters even more. Also find something unrelated to reputation that you can do for the long term, that you can keep doing even if no one applauds, because this support lasts longer than applause.

My advice: when decorating, first settle the budget. What looks good in a show flat will go half unused once it comes into your own home. At home, display few liquor cabinets or smoking items, and things that can remind you at any moment, because only when the eyes do not see will the heart be at peace. Be careful with fire and electricity, and check the sockets, gas and range hood regularly. Each week keep one fixed meal for family only; if a household is left with only gatherings, the cracks in affection grow bit by bit, and by the time you notice, it is too late.

My advice: if you want to change cities, do it early. Before setting out, settle your work, and do not quit and then go to try your luck. When you arrive, look for many people to bridge the way; groups of colleagues and gatherings of people from your hometown are worth attending, because your road outside is mostly given by people, not won by strength. If you really work on your own elsewhere, find a partner to work with, which is much steadier than carrying it alone. For business trips and travel, ordinary safety preparation is enough, and there is no need to be tense.

My advice: let your thoughts flow, and do not let them pile up. Keeping a diary, finding someone to talk with over the long term, and reading some books seriously are all outlets for you. Each week have at least one deep talk with a friend in a different industry, and speak out the analyses in your heart; that in itself is the best healing. Set a time limit on thinking, and stop when the time is up. Do not stay alone for long in a closed room; go out for a walk and change your environment, and many things you cannot think through will loosen up on their own.

My advice: remember one sentence. Someone who is easy to talk with is not necessarily suited to be a partner. If you really want to work together, write down in advance how the money is divided, how the work is split and how an exit is handled. When lending, make clear whether it is a loan or a gift. If any sibling is caught up in romantic trouble or a lawsuit, helping is fine, but do not tie your own money and career to them.

You should take the road of starting a business, or establish yourself through a skill you are good at. But find a meticulous partner who likes stability to make up for your weak points. Set yourself a rule: do not change direction before you have done something for a full three years, because accumulation that is not yet deep enough is your greatest risk. When the execution stage has lost its appeal, hand the cleaning up to someone else and go open the next door.

You should seize early the opportunities for business trips abroad, study abroad or transfers to another city. This experience is a key step toward your independence. After starting a family you can try remote work or arrange to move between two places, and do not let yourself be shut in at home. When travelling far alone, tell your family the itinerary and choose proper lodging, and at drinking parties for entertaining clients far away, try not to go alone, and make your limits clear from the start.

You should talk frankly with your child early. Talk about what it is like to like someone, how to protect one's own body, and how to spend money. You have been through all this yourself, so what you say on these matters is more convincing than anyone's; do not use the authority of a parent to force it. Set a limit on pocket money, set hours for phones and games, and make the rules first and relax them later. For specific questions about your child's health, asking a trustworthy doctor is more reliable than looking at a chart.

You should talk frankly with your child early. Talk about what it is like to like someone, how to protect oneself, and how to spend money. Set a limit on pocket money, set hours for phones and games, and make the rules first and relax them later. There is one trap to remind you of: do not impose your own way of living on your child; what you liked to play in your youth, your child may not want to play; what you find thrilling, your child may find merely noisy. For specific questions about health, see a doctor.

You should ask your parents early the things that need asking. Old family matters, their health and their plans for the future; do not wait until there is no chance to ask. Remind them to have regular health check-ups, and if they feel unwell, to see a doctor promptly and listen to the doctor. When your parents-in-law hand you tasks, it is out of trust, but do not take on every problem just to fulfil the role of a good daughter-in-law; accept what you can, and say plainly what you cannot. At work, take the initiative to find a senior woman with long experience as a mentor, which will help a great deal.

You should ask your parents early the things that need asking. Old family matters, their health and their plans for the future; do not wait until there is no chance to ask. Remind them to have regular health check-ups, and if they feel unwell, to see a doctor promptly. You get along very well with superiors of the elder generation, so take the initiative to find one with long experience as a mentor. Do not treat their expectations as a mandatory task you must complete; that you live well is already the result they hope for.

You should keep a “stay in touch often, get entangled little” relationship with your siblings. Ask after them a little more often, and keep money and business separate. If you do cooperate, do it for the short term: settle accounts once per project, divide the money when it is done and then each go your own way, which suits you better than being tied together for the long term. Whoever you cooperate with, how much money each puts in, who is responsible for which part and how the books are divided must be written down in black and white from the start; do not think that because they are relatives it is awkward to bring up.

When cooperating with family members, you should always go by a contract. How the money is divided and how the work is split should be written down in black and white; do not use affection as a contract. It is the same with loans: make clear whether it is a loan or a gift. If any sibling is caught up in romantic trouble or a lawsuit, help if you can, but do not tie your own business and money to them.

With money passing between you and friends, you should always keep the accounts square. Write the loan note with the amount and the repayment date; affection is affection, and accounts are accounts. If you truly cannot bring yourself to ask for it back, lend from the start only an amount you are willing to give away, and once lent, treat it as a gift, which actually leaves your heart at ease. When choosing subordinates, better to have slightly weaker ability but choose someone whose character can be trusted: ability can be taught, but an untrustworthy person cannot be saved.

You do not need to rush to sort out your relationship with your mother. First settle a way of living together: talk a lot about what can be talked about, avoid topics that do not fit, and do not dig up old matters every time you meet. For your elders' health, just have routine check-ups as a matter of course, and if there is a problem listen to the doctor; do not frighten yourself by looking at the chart. After marriage, basic courtesy toward your parents-in-law is enough, with no need to force closeness; your nature is hard for elders to understand, and being polite while keeping some distance will actually let you get along for longer.

You should fix a regular time for video calls with your parents. Once a week, so that your longing has an outlet and does not turn into a heavy burden on your heart. For big decisions such as going far away, give yourself two weeks before settling, and do not agree on the spot at the dinner table. Being the pillar of your husband's family is fine, but do not take on everything; leave a little for others to do.

You should talk with your parents about specific matters. Do not rake up old matters: for their affairs, first ask how they want to handle it and only then offer your opinion, and do not start correcting the moment you walk in. When you are with your mother, stop first when you are about to lose your temper, and say it at another time. In daily life, talk about many small things and lecture little; sending a photo every few days or asking whether they have eaten is more useful than long talks. After marriage, lower your expectations of your parents-in-law, keep to etiquette, and be content if things look smooth on the surface, with no need to force conversations that suit each other.

You should put your boundaries with male friends out in the open. No meeting alone late at night, no confiding private matters late at night, and keep your dealings in public places where possible. If you are married, pay even more attention: your natural friendliness is easily read by outsiders as something else, and what gets hurt is the trust at home. Sort your friends clearly: those who help you get things done, those you can do business with, and those who are only for going out with. For loans, guarantees and cooperation, let a day pass before you answer.

You should keep by your side two or three people who dare to tell you to your face when you are wrong. Every so often, look them up and talk about what you have been doing lately, and when they say something hard to hear, do not rush to explain. When lending money, draw a line for yourself: above a certain amount, never lend, and once lent, treat it as a gift. If someone keeps taking advantage of you, there is no need to fall out; seeing them less is enough.

My suggestion: at least once in your life you should go to a big city, a big platform or a foreign country. Seriously spreading your career out to a broader place is a step that is almost indispensable for you. Once you are far away, be especially careful about drinking parties and socialising; entanglements of love and money in an unfamiliar place are the hardest to clean up, so if you can avoid drinking, do not drink, and if you can bring colleagues along, do not go alone.

Before marrying far away or going on a long-term business assignment far away, you should honestly ask yourself three questions. Without your mother's family to help, can you deal on your own with the people and affairs on your husband's side? Can you make decisions and manage money by yourself? Can you raise a child to maturity on your own? If the answer to any one is no, consider further, or fill in that gap first. Before changing cities, settle your work first and only then set out.

When you go far away, you should give priority to work that has challenge. Start-ups, reform projects and technical pioneering are all fine; do not just change cities and do the old trade, because you cannot last in repetitive work. Wherever you go, do three things first as soon as you set foot there: settle your lodging, get to know two or three locals whose word carries weight, and divide your money among different accounts.

When you go far away, you should choose work that has challenge. Do not just change cities and do the old trade. As soon as you set foot there, do three things first: settle your lodging, get to know two or three locals whose word carries weight, and keep a fixed emotional outlet for yourself, even if it is only a call to an old friend at a set hour each week. If you marry far away, do not live the new life while clutching your old self, and do not run back to your mother's home at every little thing, because that would leave you stuck in the middle, wearing yourself out at both ends.

Money passing between brothers and sisters should always be recorded clearly. How much is borrowed, when it will be repaid, who puts in capital and who holds how much, write it down in black and white. The more you fear losing affection and blur the accounts, the deeper the hurt in the end. When dividing things at home, you must speak up for your own share yourself, and not count on others to think of it for you. In daily life you do not need much contact; one call a month is enough.

When the family's resources are divided, you must speak up and claim your own share. Do not wait for anyone to think of it for you. When cooperating with siblings, work project by project: how much is put in this time, how much each holds and when the accounts are settled should be written down in black and white beforehand, settling each item as it is done. It is the same with loans: write the amount and the repayment date clearly. The more you fear a rift and blur the accounts, the deeper the hurt in the end.

For a high-value decision to buy a home, you should first have a professional lawyer go over the contract once. Check each clause on ownership, mortgage and handover dates. For an older home, go and view it several more times, once in the daytime and once at night, and ask the neighbours. For the furnishings, you lean toward the lasting classical style, with solid wood furniture; a classical Chinese or European style is fine, and choose materials by the standard of not going out of date in ten years, rather than chasing the newest fashion.

Treat exercise as discipline, not as something you do only when you feel like it. Walking, hiking and the gym are all fine; put them in your weekly schedule, and the key is not to break the chain. Eat plainly and regularly, with little oil and salt, add coarse grains to your starches, and keep sweets under control. Have a regular health check-up every year, check blood sugar, blood lipids and weight carefully, and if there is a problem, handle it as the doctor directs, and do not bear it alone. For what is stuck in your heart, find someone to talk to, and do not swallow it all alone.

Treat exercise as discipline. Put it in your weekly schedule four or more times, and around the age of forty especially, do not break the chain. Eat plainly and regularly, with little oil and salt, a bit more coarse grain, and keep sweets under control. Have a regular health check-up every year, check blood sugar, blood lipids and weight carefully, plus one gynaecological examination, and let the doctor arrange exactly which items to check; at stages such as preparing for pregnancy and pregnancy, complete all the tests as directed, and listen to the doctor about diet during pregnancy as well. If you feel unwell, see a doctor promptly, and do not try to bear it alone.

Going out into the world benefits you. Buying a home in another place especially comes easily to you, and is a fairly effortless road to building up assets. When developing outside, quiet, brain-based work suits you better: culture, the arts, consulting and technology are all fine as cross-region jobs; being sent out to charge for sales figures and run around selling does not suit you. People with Sun and Moon Reversed mostly move away from the family business and leave their hometown to make a living in another land.

Going out into the world benefits you, but it also has a price. Other places give you room to develop quietly, and work such as culture, the arts, education and consulting opens up when done elsewhere, and there is often a gain in property too; the price is a heavy sense of loneliness, with no familiar person nearby to support you, so your mood easily goes down.
A delicate mind and a good eye, with moods like the moon that is sometimes full and sometimes waning.
Your mind cannot be idle and cannot be still; wearing yourself out in mind and effort is only to be expected.

Whether the heart is a weak point is not decided by matching it as “the Sun belongs to Fire”, nor by looking at the Health palace alone: across the whole chart, find the palace where malefic stars gather most and are worst, and match the organ to the earthly branch of that palace (Rat gallbladder, Ox liver, Tiger lung, Rabbit large intestine, Dragon stomach, Snake spleen, Horse heart, Goat small intestine, Monkey bladder, Rooster kidney, Dog pericardium, Pig triple burner). The Horse palace corresponds to a congenital heart condition, and the Dog palace (pericardium) to heart disease later in life; if malefic stars gather in the Horse palace or the Dog palace, have your heart checked on schedule. The Health palace is for reference only, and must be read together with the Life palace and the Decade now underway. Have regular health check-ups and follow the doctor's instructions.

Whether the heart is a weak point is not decided by matching it as “Integrity belongs to Fire”, nor by looking at the Health palace alone: across the whole chart, find the palace where malefic stars gather most and are worst, and match the organ to the earthly branch of that palace (Rat gallbladder, Ox liver, Tiger lung, Rabbit large intestine, Dragon stomach, Snake spleen, Horse heart, Goat small intestine, Monkey bladder, Rooster kidney, Dog pericardium, Pig triple burner); if two palaces are both bad, look at both places. The Health palace is for reference only, and must be read together with the Life palace and the Decade now underway. Have regular health check-ups and follow the doctor's instructions.
Only when busy do you have good fortune; as soon as you are idle, your heart feels empty.
A firm nature, not good at fitting in, relying on one skill to stand firm amid upheaval.
A fierce nature, talented in many fields, with feelings invested very deeply, needing reason to hold in check the flames of passion.
A hot temper but a soft heart, a quick mind, thinking much and doing little.
A gentle, generous and upright nature, with literary talent and also ambition, only that being too easygoing makes you prone to slackening.

A gentle and upright nature, widely knowledgeable and also flexible; beneath the generous appearance there is considerable calculation, able to hold what you have but not daring to charge ahead very much.
A fierce and decisive nature that refuses to admit defeat; when strong, you can instead build up a fortune, and it is when weak that things turn ominous.
You think too much, your heart keeps circling around matters of gossip and dispute, worry drains your strength, and you feel uneasy inside.

To break through this ceiling, do three things. At least once a year, talk plainly with your superior about a promotion or a raise; when the company discusses direction, step in and speak up on your own initiative, and do not stay only at the execution level; and outside the office, build a professional standing of your own, for example by joining a trade association, giving talks, or writing articles about your field. After returning from maternity leave, many people will assume by default that you should carry more housework and less office work; before the birth, discuss the division of tasks clearly with your family and your superior.

In love you change easily, and on-and-off relationships are fairly common; when rational you are clear-headed, and when emotional you are impulsive. The old books also say that people with this life pattern often worship the Buddha and suit a quiet path of spiritual cultivation, so most have an affinity with religion, or an interest in fate studies and philosophy. The greatest lesson of growing up is “think less and do more, curb your changeability, and focus in one place”, which means do not only think, act more, reduce the habit of changing often, and aim at one direction; the cleverness of the Strategist, if it does not turn into results, becomes a burden instead.

You have rich feelings and are gentle and considerate toward family and friends; only that you are too easygoing, easily going along with others when something comes up, and over time you may lose your own direction, needing someone beside you or circumstances to give you a push. If it is in the Temple position (strong) and meets benefic stars, you are clever, understand everything, and have no worry about food and clothing as well as a good name; Harmony is not without accomplishment, but it needs good relationships and opportunities to push it forward.

In love, you want to be the one who calls the shots. You hope your other half makes you the centre, and at the same time you are willing to give her real shelter and material support, the kind of husband who values face but also truly carries responsibility. Your love life starts rather late, and marrying a little later is likely to last longer, because you need a long enough time before you dare to commit to a person. Your wife mostly has an uncommon bearing, with her own position and views, not the kind who lives by leaning on you, and sometimes her presence is even stronger than yours. She can help you in your career, may bring you connections, and can also be a support in your heart.
Your property comes little at first and more later, mostly built with your own hands from nothing.

On matters of property, first make the ownership clear. For big matters like buying a home or transferring ownership, first ask a professional to go through the contract clause by clause and make sure the ownership is clearly written; do not mind the trouble. When quarrelling at home, each of you spend five minutes alone and then talk.

To you, a home is not just an asset but a root. You demand a great deal of peace and stability in where you live; if circumstances allow, having a space that is entirely your own will steady your whole being. This is not distrust of your partner, but a person with a character like yours simply needs a place to be alone.

A home is especially important to you. It is the place you return to, and also the steadiest foundation of your whole life. You can keep the estate your ancestors left, and the home you buy yourself also prospers. Your home is usually tidy and orderly, and being there puts people at ease; when it comes to keeping a home, you have very deep inner strength.

A home is especially important to you; it is your hardest support. The estate your ancestors left goes in a different direction with each share once it reaches your hands. Whether married or not, you tend to keep one home in your own name; this is not distrust of your other half, but your character needs money and assets in hand to feel secure. For furnishings you like things simple and practical, and you dislike anything gaudy and flowery most of all.

A home is your most practical asset, and you feel at ease only when money is put into bricks and stone. The estate your ancestors left goes in a different direction with each share in your hands. Your demands for your home are very practical too: simple, easy to clean, with things handy to reach is enough, and gaudy ornaments have no place with you.

A home is the most important part of your family fortune. You can keep the part your ancestors left, and the part you saved up and bought yourself also stays prosperous; you are especially good at taking over an existing estate and looking after it well.

A home is the most important money pouch of your life. The home you buy yourself is the most prosperous one, and counting on a home left to you is by contrast not the main line. You demand a lot of your living place: the location, the size and the furnishings must all be enough to keep up appearances, and this is also where you spend most freely.

As for property, this is the firmest foundation of your life. Having a place of your own to live first, and then slowly buying more, is the smoothest way for you to accumulate money. A home matters more to you than career and social life, and whether things are peaceful at home directly decides how much strength you have outside.

On matters of property you basically rely on yourself. What is left to you is limited, so you are a little cramped when young, and only from middle age onward does it gradually become more spacious. You have a very high gift for making a life: an eye for choosing things, a talent for turning everyday living into ritual, and an atmosphere that makes people want to stay once they step through the door are all your strengths. After marriage you are very well suited to be the centre of the household, organising holidays and hosting relatives and friends, and these tasks give you a particular sense of achievement. When Taboo (obstruction) is in effect, money all goes into enjoyment, and the home never manages to accumulate anything.

On matters of property, you must rely on yourself. The family fortune of your ancestors cannot be kept once it reaches you. The atmosphere at home matters just as much: the moment the family sits down and talks everything through is the most comfortable, and the time of daily quarrels over small things drains your spirit most.

On matters of property, you must rely on yourself. The family fortune of your ancestors cannot be kept once it reaches you. The atmosphere at home matters just as much: the moment of sitting down and talking everything through is the most comfortable, the time of daily quarrels over small things is the most hurtful, and the stories between mother-in-law and daughter-in-law and between mother and daughter drain your spirit most.

So do not understand Treasury only as “knows how to keep but not how to earn”; the meaning is that it both keeps money and earns money. Volume one also says that meeting Wealth Keeper and Martial accumulates a very large fortune. The case of Treasury with Heavenly Horse in the Spouse palace speaks of your spouse: the Treasury star is good at managing money, generous, and willing to work hard; while the money-managing nature of this star, when it falls in the Wealth palace, speaks of your own ability to manage money: the skill of managing money together with willingness to work is the true road of wealth for Treasury. Mainly arrange things in a steady direction, and with long-term accumulation your foundation will be very thick.
You hold real power; when Seven Killings is strong, you shine most in positions of real power such as the military and the police, and leisurely office work does not suit you.

Use your eye for choosing things when buying a home. Look at the location, the neighbourhood and the layout of the apartment; your meticulousness gains you a great deal here. With your partner, talk about money clearly: whose name the home is in, how daily expenses are divided, and above what amount a spending needs discussion, all said clearly beforehand. Before making a large payment for family, do one calculation: will this outflow touch the money set aside for your old age? Invest in the steady direction, and touch little that fluctuates sharply; from middle age onward, the value of your home will gradually show.

Put more effort into creating conditions for your child. Do not decide for your child; the good school, good environment and good opportunities that you win are far more useful than telling your child outright what to choose. When your child enters middle school, start practising letting go, speaking less and watching more, and what your child can decide alone, hand over more and more year after year. If you do end up quarrelling, you step back first, and talk when both have cooled. Besides, leave the postpartum month to professionals, and do not push through it.

Put time alone into your schedule seriously. Not leaving it free only when you have spare time, but setting it aside first. When your mood is low, do not suppress it; write it out, tell someone trustworthy, and let it flow away. From middle age onward you can take up quiet practices: sitting meditation, gentle yoga and long solitary walks are all good for you. One more thing: this age praises outward brilliance, but your quiet refinement is not a flaw, it is your strength.

Close the door firmly between life and work, and do not bring family matters into the office. Prepare a list for low days, so that on days when you are in poor shape you do only three or five items on it, and do not let your emotions drag down the whole body of work. If you plan to have a child, arrange childcare in advance, and do not hold on alone; the period of returning to work will then be far less of a tug of war. After forty you can go in a more self-directed direction, such as designer or consultant, trades that live on expertise, but underneath there should still be a stable income to support you.

Make steady income the main line and the home the foundation. From middle age onward, the value of this part will gradually show. For large expenses, decide after a night, and do not sign while in the grip of emotion. Invest in what is solid and low in volatility, and touch financial speculation with high swings little. Before taking money out for family, do one calculation: will this outflow touch your own capital? Your wife's income has a very large bearing on your financial fortune; looking after the relationship well is itself looking after the money.

For investing, you suit the steady kind. Choose a home to live in and a property to rent out, or projects whose returns you can see clearly, and do not touch high-risk speculation. Money leaks easily in three places: unexpected costs for medical care and accidents, tangled and unclear accounts with other people, and constantly paying out for people in your love life. Set aside a dedicated reserve fund, and for cooperation and loans always write everything down in black and white. If you do cooperate, a form in which others put in the money and you step forward to lead suits you better.

Choose one field and dig deep, build a reputation, and your income will naturally be steady. If you really want to work for yourself, choose a small but refined direction, such as a personal brand, design or consulting, and do not enter industries that need heavy capital and a race for speed. You are good at looking after other people's feelings, but disagreements that need voicing must still be voiced, or in time no one will take you seriously. You care too much about how people judge you, and one remark can leave you unsettled for the whole session; gather the comments you care about in one place and look at them once at a fixed time, and do not take them in all the time.

Choose your field correctly. Culture, the arts, media, consulting and education are fields that need refinement and suit you; face-to-face selling and work that relies on physical force should not be forced on yourself. Put your most important tasks into a quiet time slot. One more thing that is more important: you too want to be cared for, only you have never spoken up; from now on, say plainly what you want, and do not wait for the other person to guess. There is no need to force yourself to become extroverted; your refinement is worth a great deal to those who know how to recognise it.

The family estate you have received, first hold it steady. Do not let the home stay cold and desolate for long: open the windows more, add lights, and invite siblings and friends to sit and visit more often. When there is enough human warmth, the feeling of living there will be completely different.
The family estate you have received, first hold it steady. Do not let the home stay cold and desolate for long: open the windows more, and invite friends to sit and visit more often.

Your income is not very fixed, and it is hard to predict how much will come in next month. Whether to be your own boss depends on whether Power and Prosperity meet in the Wealth palace (Wealth Keeper also counts as Prosperity). You spend freely, and the costs of entertaining guests, giving gifts and keeping up appearances are clearly high; this is where most of your money drains away. Money often comes late, and only from middle age onward does it become plentiful.
Suited to both civil and martial work, with no shortage of income; sharing the palace with Emperor, the “Complete Book” says “with Emperor, powerful and noble”.
Capable in both civil and martial work, with face fully secured; the Minister entry in the “Complete Book” says “with Integrity, brilliant, powerful and noble”.
A comfortable life, enjoying good fortune and living long; when meeting malefic stars, you cannot be at peace.

Star combinations need to be told apart. When Integrity and Army Breaker sit together in the Rabbit or Rooster palace, the traditional reading is a disaster connected with water; this reading must also be checked against the lines on the tip of the person's own nose, and no conclusion is drawn without actually seeing the person. The original line in the “Tai Wei Rhapsody” says that Army Breaker sharing a palace with Great Gate means “water is the grave”, and it speaks of Army Breaker meeting Great Gate. Integrity and Greedy Wolf together in the Fallen position is called “Half-Empty, Broken Wing”; the danger lies in middle age and there may be a premature loss midway, but this is only a rough principle; this combination leans toward congenital illness, such as being born with a hard-to-cure disease, along with a tendency to harm oneself. Integrity with Seven Killings was called in the old days “buried by the roadside”, which is also a heavy saying of the ancients, meant to remind you to leave yourself a way out when you act; but it has to be judged by position: only the Fallen position is ominous, while in the Temple position (strong force) it can instead make you the leader of a region, and the “Bone Marrow Rhapsody” also says “Integrity with Seven Killings is, on the contrary, a person who accumulates wealth”, meaning this combination can in fact build a fortune.
A later marriage brings harmony, while marrying too early tends to cause problems instead.
Marrying a little later brings peace, while marrying early invites clashes; your partner is strong-natured and neither of you gives way to the other.

The best combination is meeting the Fire Star or the Bell Star, called the “**Fire Star with Greedy Wolf**” pattern or the “**Bell Star with Greedy Wolf**” pattern, which tends to bring a sudden large windfall; the old books also say “only meeting the Fire Star and Bell Star brings wealth and rank”, meaning that only by meeting the Fire Star and Bell Star can you rise; but note that this kind of pattern rises fast and falls fast, and if it is clashed by malefic stars such as the Ram Blade and Hindrance, you are instead prone to wearing down your body through drink and lust.

What you most need to guard against is excessive empathy. You will take your child's feelings entirely onto yourself, and as a result mother and child drain each other. When your child cries, tell yourself inwardly: this is my child's feeling, not my responsibility. You do not need to pay the price for every emotion your daughter has; listening to her fully and staying by her side is enough, so do not rush to solve things in her place. During the postpartum confinement, let your family take care of you and do not force yourself to hold up; if you recover well this one month, you will have much more strength in the years that follow.

What deserves the most attention is that a child who is too well-behaved easily lacks opinions of their own and lacks the drive to charge ahead. Growing up, they wait for others to arrange everything. From an early age you should hand over part of the power of choice: which class to take, how to spend the weekend, how to arrange the room, let your child decide, and when the choice is wrong let your child bear it once; do not decide everything for your child. When your child says “anything is fine”, ask one more question about which one they really want.

What you most need to guard against is closing a business deal at the drinking table. A few cups down and you agree at once, and the next day when you are sober you find the terms were never properly discussed. Set a hard rule: do not sign or transfer money after drinking, and review the terms the next day. If you do genuinely cooperate, selling goods, food and drink, entertainment and running a platform suit you best, and the accounts and the sharing of profits must be written into the contract from the very start. In ordinary days, making a few extra calls to ask after people is more useful than laying on a big banquet at festivals.
You suit most the positions that do real work, such as the army or the police, and with good conditions you may even hold great power.
When the Moon is bright you are relaxed and cheerful; when the Moon is dim or meets malefic stars, there is a lot of sorrow and unrest.

There is one point to arrange early. The things the elders in the family have promised, and the housing and contracts of older people, are best written down in black and white while everyone is still clear-headed; do not count on a spoken word being enough. When your parents grow older, take them for regular health check-ups, and do not wait until something happens before rushing to the hospital. At work you suit best a strong superior whose words carry weight; you can actively look for a leader willing to guide you, and if you follow the right person your career gets a very clear boost.
With help from benefic stars you can make a sum of money; money that comes fast also goes fast.
You have good fortune and a comfortable life; if the Ram Blade, Hindrance, Bell Star, Earth Void and Earth Robbery are added, the “Complete Book” says “thin blessings”.
Friends and subordinates who complain a lot do not stay long, and a single remark can turn them into enemies.
Friends and subordinates are virtuous and willing to put in effort, and the people who serve as your right-hand helpers in this palace are especially plentiful.
Desires are many, talents are broad, and you are strong-willed yet stubborn; whether you succeed or fail depends on whether you can govern yourself.

Precisely because things are too stable, the warmth tends to fade gradually over time. Do not take not quarrelling to mean that everything is fine. Each week you should set aside a stretch of time just for the two of you, even if it is only sharing a meal or taking a walk; for what she does for you, say a direct thank you, and do not assume she already knows. If you want to meet more people, go ahead and boldly ask acquaintances to introduce someone; this route is the most effective for you.
Regular income is steady, you manage money with a method, and you neither speculate nor take risks.
Martial + Right Assistant means capable subordinates: the source of money is stable and debts are collected smoothly. It suits businesses with cash flow (trade, food and drink, retail chains).

Martial + Earth Robbery means money is robbed: at least once in life there is a major financial loss (a bad investment that turns out to be a scam, a partner who runs off with the money, being cheated).
Martial + Earth Void means the treasury is emptied: however much you earn you cannot keep it, so you need a forced savings mechanism, regular investing and automatic deductions.
Martial + Heavenly Halberd means a female noble helper who aids you with money: a female investor or a senior woman leader may become the turning point of your wealth fortune.
Martial + Heavenly Leader means a male noble helper who helps you earn big money: a male elder or a boss may, with a single boost, change the direction of your wealth fortune.

Martial + Left Assistant means the energy of wealth plus a team: you not only earn strongly but can also lead a team to earn together. It suits being a sales director, head of a business line, or building a startup team geared toward creating wealth.
Martial + Ram Blade is the classic ominous pattern “Martial and Ram”: in a woman's chart it means damage to marriage, in a man's chart it means seeing blood, injuries and punishment.

Martial + Literary Talent means earning money through reason: you rely not on impulse but on professional judgment and data-driven decisions. It suits financial analysts, investment bankers and tax or audit specialists best.

Martial + Literary Arts means earning money through negotiation: you can create wealth through your eloquence and your ability to close deals. Head of a business division, merger and acquisition adviser, and commercial lawyer are the best.

Martial + Fire Star means money comes and goes fiercely: you may suddenly get rich or suddenly lose heavily. For health, watch the respiratory system (Fire overcomes Metal, prone to heat in the lungs and rhinitis).
Martial + Bell Star, like the Fire Star, means fierce energy of wealth, but it leans more toward being hidden - you are prone to putting everything on a single gamble in investing.
Martial + Hindrance means delayed wealth fortune: good opportunities are missed through hesitation, and the habit of “wait and see” makes you half a beat slower than others.

Martial “when the four malefic stars clash and break it, one is lonely and poor, to varying degrees”, meaning that when it is clashed and broken by the Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star and Bell Star, you may be lonely or poor but upright, to an uneven degree. Even when clashed and broken, Treasury still “governs full money, goods and land”, meaning wealth and property are not lacking. With malefic stars, the path of money meets obstacles but the family estate remains. Treasury has no power to block disaster, so do not count on it to block trouble. This life pattern values real gain and easily underrates feelings.

Martial with Seven Killings sitting together in the Life palace, a wealth star paired with a general star, is called “a martial general who manages money”, meaning like a general guarding the money. Martial is “firm-natured and decisive”, meaning hard-natured and quick to settle matters; Seven Killings “acts with advancing and retreating in quiet thought”, meaning you often think before and after and weigh going forward against going back; so you dare to decide, you are quick and resolute, but when facing a matter you may also waver. The “Complete Book” says “Martial and Seven Killings in the Life palace in the Temple or Prosperous position”, meaning the two stars sit in the Life palace in a strong position. Seven Killings is a general star, and sitting in the Life palace it easily makes a military officer; the military or police, law and diplomacy suit best; Martial is the foremost wealth star, and holding financial power also works. A lifetime of toil and hardship, with the risk lying in being too rigid and so easily breaking; the “Complete Book” also warns of Martial “with Seven Killings and the Fire Star in the same palace, robbed because of money”, meaning you are prone to being schemed against over money and losing it, and when contending for profit you must guard against being bitten back. A general star falling in a woman's chart makes the craving for power too heavy; using that strength in a career is better.

Martial with Seven Killings sitting together in the Life palace, a wealth star paired with a general star, is called “a martial general who manages money”, meaning like a general guarding the money. Martial is “firm-natured and decisive”, meaning hard-natured and quick to settle matters; Seven Killings “acts with advancing and retreating in quiet thought”, meaning you often think before and after and weigh going forward against going back; so you dare to decide, you are quick and resolute, but when facing a matter you may also waver. The “Complete Book” says “Martial and Seven Killings in the Life palace in the Temple or Prosperous position”, meaning the two stars sit in the Life palace in a strong position. Seven Killings is a general star, and sitting in the Life palace it easily makes a military officer; the military or police, law and diplomacy suit best; Martial is the foremost wealth star, and holding financial power also works. A lifetime of toil and hardship, with the risk lying in being too rigid and so easily breaking; the “Complete Book” also warns of Martial “with Seven Killings and the Fire Star in the same palace, robbed because of money”, meaning you are prone to being schemed against over money and losing it, and when contending for profit you must guard against being bitten back. For a woman's chart: the ancient books say this person “acts decisively and is also clever”, meaning she handles things resolutely and has a quick mind, only that hardship is hard to avoid and her feelings are also easily hurt; a general star falling in a woman's chart makes the craving for power too heavy, and using that strength in a career is better.

Martial with Seven Killings sitting in the Spouse palace means a marriage with many setbacks. The “Complete Book” says Martial “clashes with the partner so marry late”, meaning Martial here easily brings conflict, and marrying a little later is good; it says Seven Killings “harms early, and Martial in the same palace also harms, or marry late and you escape punishment”, meaning that marrying early hurts the relationship and marrying late brings harmony. Your partner is hot-tempered, stubborn and suspicious; this person is distrustful and doubts everything they see, so living together is tiring and you need to leave plenty of distance. With benefic stars, you may instead gain money through your partner; with the Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void and Earth Robbery, the damage to the relationship is heavier. The original text under Martial in the “Wives and Concubines” chapter of the “Complete Book” is “with benefic stars added, one gains property through the wife; if ominous, marrying a wife loses one's livelihood”; as for the level of meeting malefic stars, the original text does not say whether they share the palace or shine on it from the trine palaces, nor does it distinguish bright from dim, so you must also look at which star it is and how they meet.

Martial with Seven Killings sitting in the Career palace suits the path of real power. The “Complete Book” says Martial in the Career palace “with Seven Killings settling the Body together, jointly establishes a name and rank”, meaning the Body palace also falls in this palace and shares the palace with Seven Killings, so rank and reputation rely on charging forward; it says of Seven Killings “in the Temple or Prosperous position, a military post is glorious and the power and rank are not small, unsuited to scholars, and Martial in the same palace has power and rank too”, meaning that when Seven Killings is strong, the military path is outstanding and the authority is considerable, and Martial sharing the palace is the same; it is unsuited to purely desk work: the military or police, law and diplomacy, trades that need decisiveness, are the ones that fit. When Martial is strong, holding financial power also works. With Hindrance, Bell Star and Earth Robbery, the “Complete Book” also says “no share in rank and fame”.

Martial with Seven Killings sitting in the Wealth palace follows the path of building from nothing. The “Complete Book” says Martial meeting Seven Killings means “making wealth with empty hands and founding a household”, meaning you earn a livelihood from bare hands; money does not rely on family capital but has to be earned by yourself. Seven Killings and Army Breaker govern waste, scattering and hard labour, so money comes in and then goes out, and the more comes in, the faster it disperses. With the Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star and Bell Star it “does not gather, and fears the Void most of all”, meaning money is even harder to keep, and the greatest fear is meeting empty stars such as Earth Void and Earth Robbery on top of that.
Martial governs the Wealth and Property palaces in particular, and real estate is an important asset for you.

Martial in the Temple position (especially in the four Tomb palaces Dragon, Dog, Ox and Goat, where it is even more prosperous) guarding the Wealth palace means the wealth star is developed to the extreme in its own seat. It is a genuine image of a “thick and solid treasury”, good both at earning and keeping money, so you should centre your arrangements on real-economy business or hard assets.

Martial transforming to Power in the Wealth palace or its trine palaces holds the power over money: you are born with the ability to be a boss, to run a household and manage money, and the authority over finances sits firmly in your hands. The old verse says “Martial transforming to Power, heads the household and founds a business of one's own”, so start your own business or take the post of finance director or CFO in a company; your initiative in directing money is the greatest code of your wealth.

Martial transforming to Power in the Life palace holds money with the proper way, your control over finances is very strong, and both your desire and your ability to be your own boss reach the highest level. You should start your own business or be the person in charge of a company's finances, which is a superb pattern for starting a business.

Martial transforming to Power: a wealth star, one of the strongest wealth stars, firm and decisive, good at managing money and doing business; it is glad to have the Wealth Keeper in the same palace and fears being restrained and falling into the Fallen position.

Martial transforming to Prosperity in the Wealth palace or its trine palaces, the wealth star transformed to Prosperity, is to say “the wealth star gaining Prosperity”, the strongest great-wealth pattern among the 14 main stars: Martial is the wealth star, and when it transforms to Prosperity the wealth star gains even more Prosperity, the sources of money open wide and flow in naturally; finance, real-economy business, asset management and real estate investment are all the most prosperous paths for money. A Life with this pattern should boldly expand the map of its career, and the speed of accumulating wealth far exceeds that of peers.

Martial transforming to Prosperity in the Career palace or its trine palaces, the path of money is wide open; Prosperity in the Career palace may point to managing public money or an institution's money in a post, and holding money does not mean the money belongs to you.

Martial transforming to Prosperity in the Life palace, the wealth star gaining Prosperity, is the strongest great-wealth pattern among the 14 main stars: money comes in extreme abundance, and running your own business or heading a finance department are both greatly auspicious; finance, industry and asset management can all bring great achievements.

Martial transforming to Prosperity, the path of romance runs smoothly: you use actions and wealth to exchange for emotional stability, your partner admires your real strength, the marriage is steady through striving together, and a financial foundation is the greatest support of the relationship.

Martial transforming to Prosperity: a wealth star, one of the strongest wealth stars, firm and decisive, good at managing money and doing business; it is glad to have the Wealth Keeper in the same palace and fears being restrained and falling into the Fallen position.

Martial and Minister sitting together in the Life palace: a wealth star (governing money) paired with a seal star, where the seal means holding the stamp and handling approvals. Martial is firm-natured, quick to decide, straightforward in heart and without ill intent; Minister speaks in a practical way and steps in to defend anyone he sees being bullied. So a person with this life pattern acts fairly and by principle, and their ability to manage money is also especially strong. The seal star Minister makes Martial's handling of money more orderly and more respectful of rules, and suits sitting in a post that manages money and approvals.

Martial and Greedy Wolf sitting together in the Life palace: a wealth star (governing money) paired with a Peach Blossom star (governing romantic affinity), is a typical late-blooming pattern. The “Complete Book” says “Greedy Wolf does not bring success to a young man”, meaning Greedy Wolf does not let a person prosper when young; the “Bone Marrow Rhapsody” says “Greedy Wolf and Martial in the Tomb palace, blessings come only at thirty”, meaning that when these two stars sit in the Tomb palace, the luck of blessings begins only at the age of thirty. So before thirty it is mostly toil and running about, and afterwards the accumulated strength is converted into results all at once.

A person with Martial in the Life palace is a typical practical doer: clear goals, strong execution, dislikes empty talk and looks only at results. The “Complete Book”, in the “Rhapsody on Form and Nature”, says of Martial that it “is a very essential character, with a resolute temperament”, meaning that in work you grasp the most critical link and your temperament is decisive, so whatever the matter you seize the key point and act fast, with high demands on yourself and others, and sometimes you seem strict. Martial's temper is like the Sun's: when it explodes it explodes, but once it has exploded it is over, and no debt is carried overnight. Whether Martial in the Life palace forms a pattern also depends on one more physical condition: whether the body has the build of the “five short features”. This is one point where the physical appearance is checked against the Life, and it must be checked directly; until it is checked, whether this pattern forms is left open for now, and no conclusion is drawn on your behalf.
Martial sitting in the treasury knows how to earn and also how to keep, and with malefic stars there are ups and downs.

Martial and Treasury sitting together in the Life palace: a wealth star paired with a storehouse star. The “Complete Book” says Martial “is the master of the Wealth palace”, meaning it governs money and goods; it says Treasury “is the storehouse of wealth, and a Life that meets it ends up rich”, meaning Treasury is like a money vault, and a Life palace that meets it is rich in the end, able to earn and able to keep. Volume one also has the line “sharing a palace with Treasury brings longevity”, meaning that a person sharing the palace has a steady lifespan.

Martial and Treasury sitting in the Spouse palace: your partner is practical and calm, good at managing the household and money, not romantic but reliable. The “Complete Book”, in the “Wives and Concubines” section, says of Treasury “mutual generation, and one is loved and cherished”, meaning you suit each other and your partner is fond of you; it says of Martial “clashes with the partner so marry late, and a couple of the same age is also well matched”, meaning Martial here easily brings conflict, marrying a little later makes it steady, and the same age is also a good match. It also says “with benefic stars added, one gains property through the wife; if ominous, marrying a wife loses one's livelihood”, meaning with benefic stars money comes in through your partner, and with ominous stars you lose wealth because of your partner. Treasury meeting the Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void and Earth Robbery also suits a later marriage, to avoid damage to the relationship. The original text under Treasury is “meeting the Ram, Hindrance, Fire, Bell, Void and Robbery, marry late and escape punishment”, and it does not say whether they share the palace or shine on it from the trine palaces, nor does it distinguish bright from dim, so you must also look at which star it is and how they meet.

Martial and Treasury sitting in the Career palace suit work connected with money: banking, securities, accounting, corporate finance. Treasury is a civil-official star and a teaching star, and many become civil servants or teachers; Martial represents the military official, so the military or police also work. The “Complete Book”, in the Career section, says of Treasury “with Integrity and Martial, power and rank”, meaning that sharing the palace with Integrity and Martial you hold power and have standing; it also says “meeting Void and Robbery, it is mediocre”, meaning that meeting Earth Void and Earth Robbery it becomes ordinary. A career in this palace relies on solid accumulation.

Martial and Treasury sitting in the Wealth palace is a top-grade position for wealth: Martial earns, Treasury keeps, spending is restrained and investment is long-term. The old books say “Treasury and Martial in the palace of wealth and home, and also carrying power and Prosperity, make a lavish rich man”, meaning that sitting in the Wealth and Property palaces and also having benefic transformations, you are a wealthy man who dares to spend. You must also meet Transformation to Power (holding power), Transformation to Prosperity (money coming in) and the Wealth Keeper to count as greatly wealthy. Treasury “meeting the Ram, Hindrance, Fire, Bell, Void and Robbery has success and failure”, meaning that when it meets the Ram Blade, Hindrance, Fire Star, Bell Star, Earth Void and Earth Robbery, money rises and falls, and keeping is the main thing.

Martial and Treasury sitting in the Wealth palace is a top-grade position for wealth: Martial earns, Treasury keeps, spending is restrained and investment is long-term.
